accessibilityGaps: Selection affordance is undefined (entire card vs radio/button), so keyboard interaction pattern and semantic role/aria-checked labeling are missing
Delete control accessible name and semantics are unspecified (icon-only vs text), including aria-label and confirmation messaging for screen readers
Focus management is undefined (visible focus ring on card and delete, focus order, and where focus goes after deletion)
No guidance on preventing accidental activation when delete is inside a selectable card (keyboard and pointer event separation)
Card brand icon alternative text/aria-hidden behavior is not specified (decorative vs informative)
Text announced format is unspecified for masked number and expiry (e.g., reading out asterisks vs 'ending in 1234', 'expires 05/27')
missingStates: Selected state visual styling for the active card (border/background/check indicator) is not defined
Hover/pressed states for the card container and delete action are not defined
Disabled/non-interactive state (e.g., cannot select or cannot delete) is not defined
Delete confirmation state/workflow (confirm/cancel) is not defined for a destructive action
Deleting in-progress/loading state is not defined (spinner, disabling controls, preventing double submit)
Delete failure/error state is not defined (error message placement, retry behavior)
Edge case state for expired card (expiry in past) is not defined (labeling/styling/warnings)
Missing/unknown brand icon state is not defined (fallback icon/text)
recommendations: Specify the selection UI pattern (radio-style list item vs clickable card button) and define required ARIA (role, aria-checked/selected) plus keyboard behavior (Enter/Space to select)
Define destructive delete flow: inline confirmation (e.g., modal/popover) with confirm/cancel labels, and ensure delete is a distinct button to avoid triggering selection
Add explicit interaction states: default/hover/active/focus/selected/disabled for both the card container and delete action, mapped to design tokens
Define async behaviors for delete: disable delete while pending, show progress indicator, handle success removal animation, and show error with retry
Provide screen-reader-friendly strings for masked number and expiry (e.g., 'Visa ending in 1234, expires 05/27, John Doe') and mark brand icon decorative if redundant
Document focus rules: initial focus target, focus ring styling, and post-delete focus placement (next card, previous card, or list container)
responsiveGaps: Layout behavior for narrow widths is unspecified (stacking order of brand icon, number, expiry, name, and delete action)
Text overflow/truncation rules are missing for long cardholder names and small containers (ellipsis vs wrap, max lines)
Placement of delete action on mobile is undefined (right-aligned, overflow menu, second row) and how it avoids accidental taps
Minimum touch target sizes and spacing between selectable area and delete control are not specified for mobile
Handling of RTL locales is unspecified (icon/fields alignment and delete placement mirroring)

coveredBehaviors: Selecting a card from a composed list updates selected state (aria-pressed) on the targeted PaymentCard and clears it from others via parent state
Delete action is a distinct nested control that does not trigger parent card selection due to stopped event propagation
Delete confirmation opens and can be cancelled without crashing; cancelling returns the UI to its prior state and keeps focus stable
Async delete pending disables both card selection and delete action until resolution
Delete success removes the PaymentCard from the DOM and moves focus to the next card in the list (or fallback as available)
Delete failure keeps the card in the DOM, re-enables controls, and shows an inline error message; retry requires confirmation again and can succeed
coveredStates: list: one-selected (single selection in parent state)

decisions.decision: Implement selection as a single focusable control on the card container using a native <button type="button"> with aria-pressed to represent selected state (true when selected, false otherwise). Activate selection on Enter/Space and click/tap anywhere on the card excluding the delete control.
decisions.rationale: This defines an unambiguous keyboard and screen reader interaction model without requiring an external radiogroup context, while still supporting a clear selected/unselected toggle state for a dumb card component.
decisions.sourceGap: Selection affordance is undefined (entire card vs radio/button), so keyboard interaction pattern and semantic role/aria-checked labeling are missing

decisions.decision: Render delete as a separate <button type="button"> inside the card. Prevent delete from triggering card selection by stopping event propagation on pointer/click and by handling keyboard activation only when the delete button itself is focused.
decisions.rationale: This conservatively avoids accidental selection when a destructive control is nested inside a selectable container and cleanly separates semantics and event handling for both controls.
decisions.sourceGap: No guidance on preventing accidental activation when delete is inside a selectable card (keyboard and pointer event separation)

decisions.decision: Use an icon-only delete button with an accessible name via aria-label in the form "Delete card ending in {last4}". Provide a confirmation step with two explicit actions labeled "Cancel" and "Delete"; ensure confirmation content includes the same card identifier text.
decisions.rationale: This provides a deterministic accessible name for an icon-only control and defines confirmation messaging/labels required for a destructive action, while reusing last4 to avoid exposing full PAN.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete control accessible name and semantics are unspecified (icon-only vs text), including aria-label and confirmation messaging for screen readers

decisions.decision: Define focus order as: card container first, then delete button. Use visible focus styling on both via :focus-visible. After a successful deletion, programmatically move focus to the next payment_card in the list; if none exists, focus the previous; if list becomes empty, focus the parent list container (or the closest stable ancestor provided by the host).
decisions.rationale: This resolves undefined focus management and ensures keyboard users are not stranded after DOM removal; the next/previous fallback is a standard conservative pattern for deletions in lists.
decisions.sourceGap: Focus management is undefined (visible focus ring on card and delete, focus order, and where focus goes after deletion)

decisions.decision: Treat the card brand icon as decorative by default: render with empty alt (alt="") for or aria-hidden="true" for inline SVG. The accessible brand text must be included in the payment_card accessible label (not on the icon).
decisions.rationale: This prevents duplicate announcements while still ensuring the brand is conveyed once through the overall card label, which is the most stable and testable approach.
decisions.sourceGap: Card brand icon alternative text/aria-hidden behavior is not specified (decorative vs informative)

decisions.decision: Do not rely on reading visible masked characters. Provide an explicit accessible label for the payment_card in the format: "{Brand} card ending in {last4}, expires {MM}/{YY}, {CardholderName}". Keep the visible masked number as "•••• •••• •••• {last4}" (or "**** **** **** {last4}") but exclude the mask characters from the accessible label.
decisions.rationale: This avoids screen readers announcing asterisks/bullets and standardizes the spoken output using non-sensitive identifiers, resolving ambiguity about announced formats.
decisions.sourceGap: Text announced format is unspecified for masked number and expiry (e.g., reading out asterisks vs 'ending in 1234', 'expires 05/27')

decisions.decision: Implement and expose the following visual states with distinct styling hooks: payment_card: default, hover, active/pressed, focus-visible, selected, disabled. delete_card_action: default, hover, active/pressed, focus-visible, disabled. Selected state must include a clear indicator (e.g., 2px border + subtle background) in addition to any shadow change.
decisions.rationale: This defines the missing interaction/selected/disabled states in a way that downstream token mapping can implement consistently without inventing new behaviors beyond standard state sets.
decisions.sourceGap: Selected state visual styling for the active card (border/background/check indicator) is not defined

decisions.decision: Implement delete confirmation as an inline anchored dialog/popover tied to the delete button (not a full-screen modal). The dialog contains a short prompt text and two buttons (Cancel, Delete). Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the delete button; clicking outside also closes.
decisions.rationale: This concretely defines the confirm/cancel workflow and accessibility behavior while minimizing layout disruption in a dashboard list context.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete confirmation state/workflow (confirm/cancel) is not defined for a destructive action

decisions.decision: During deletion request: disable both the delete button and card selection, show a small inline spinner inside the delete button (replacing the icon), and prevent repeated submissions. On success, remove the payment_card from the DOM after a short 150–200ms collapse/fade transition.
decisions.rationale: This defines a deterministic pending and success behavior that prevents double-submit and gives immediate feedback without requiring additional UI components.
decisions.sourceGap: Deleting in-progress/loading state is not defined (spinner, disabling controls, preventing double submit)

decisions.decision: On delete failure: keep the payment_card visible, re-enable controls, and render an inline error message below the card content area (within payment_card) reading "Could not delete this card. Try again." Provide a Retry action by reusing the delete button (same confirmation step required again).
decisions.rationale: This establishes placement and copy for error feedback and a conservative retry path without introducing new controls beyond the existing delete action.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete failure/error state is not defined (error message placement, retry behavior)

decisions.decision: If the expiry date is in the past, mark the payment_card as "Expired" by adding a small text badge next to the expiry value and applying a subdued/alert text color to the expiry field. Selection remains allowed unless the host disables it via the disabled prop/state.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the undefined expired edge case while keeping behavior conservative by not forcing business logic (blocking selection) into the component.
decisions.sourceGap: Edge case state for expired card (expiry in past) is not defined (labeling/styling/warnings)

decisions.decision: If brand is missing/unknown, render a generic card icon in card_brand_icon and include brand text "Card" in the payment_card accessible label in place of the specific brand.
decisions.rationale: This provides a deterministic fallback for both visuals and accessibility without requiring additional assets or conditional layouts.
decisions.sourceGap: Missing/unknown brand icon state is not defined (fallback icon/text)

decisions.decision: For narrow widths, use a two-row layout: Row 1: brand icon (start), masked number (flex), delete button (end). Row 2: cardholder name (start) and expiry (end). Keep delete right-aligned in row 1 to remain discoverable; increase spacing around it to reduce accidental taps.
decisions.rationale: This explicitly defines responsive stacking order and delete placement without introducing menus, keeping the component predictable across breakpoints.
decisions.sourceGap: Layout behavior for narrow widths is unspecified (stacking order of brand icon, number, expiry, name, and delete action)

decisions.decision: Apply single-line truncation with ellipsis for cardholder_name and card_number_masked in constrained widths. Do not wrap. Ensure full values remain available via the payment_card accessible label (and optionally the title attribute on truncated text).
decisions.rationale: This resolves overflow ambiguity with a conservative, commonly expected dashboard behavior and keeps row heights stable in lists.
decisions.sourceGap: Text overflow/truncation rules are missing for long cardholder names and small containers (ellipsis vs wrap, max lines)

decisions.decision: Enforce minimum 44x44px touch target for both the selectable payment_card hit area and the delete button. Maintain at least 8px spacing between the delete button hit box and the nearest selectable-content hit area boundary to reduce accidental taps.
decisions.rationale: This defines concrete mobile ergonomics requirements and reduces risk of mis-taps when delete is adjacent to a large selectable surface.
decisions.sourceGap: Minimum touch target sizes and spacing between selectable area and delete control are not specified for mobile

decisions.decision: Support RTL by using logical CSS properties and mirroring layout: brand icon aligns to inline-start, delete aligns to inline-end, and the row-2 arrangement (name vs expiry) uses inline-start/inline-end alignment rather than left/right.
decisions.rationale: This resolves RTL ambiguity with a standard, minimal implementation approach that requires no extra design variants.
decisions.sourceGap: Handling of RTL locales is unspecified (icon/fields alignment and delete placement mirroring)

flows.completionCriteria: The intended payment_card is in selected state (aria-pressed=true) and visually shows selected styling/indicator; all other cards remain unselected.
flows.name: Select a saved payment card

steps.action: Click/tap the payment card container to select it (excluding the delete button area).
steps.expectedResult: The card becomes selected with selected styling and aria-pressed=true; selection change does not trigger deletion UI.

flows.completionCriteria: The targeted payment_card is deleted successfully, removed from the DOM after a brief collapse/fade, and keyboard focus is moved to the next card (or previous, or parent list container if none remain).
flows.name: Delete a saved card (confirm, async success)

steps.action: Click the delete icon button on the card.
steps.expectedResult: An anchored inline confirmation dialog/popover opens; focus remains within the confirmation UI; card selection is not triggered due to event propagation being stopped.

steps.action: Click the confirmation button labeled "Delete".
steps.expectedResult: Deletion request starts; delete button shows an inline spinner; both delete and card selection are disabled to prevent repeated submissions.

steps.action: Wait for the delete request to resolve successfully.
steps.expectedResult: The payment_card collapses/fades out over ~150–200ms then is removed from the DOM; focus is moved to the next payment_card in the list, else previous, else the parent list container/closest stable ancestor.

flows.completionCriteria: User successfully selects one card, then successfully deletes a (possibly different) card via confirmation; focus management behaves as specified after deletion.
flows.name: Explore card states, then select and delete

steps.action: Use keyboard Tab to move focus to a payment card container.
steps.expectedResult: Visible :focus-visible styling appears on the payment_card; screen reader announces the explicit label: "{Brand} card ending in {last4}, expires {MM}/{YY}, {CardholderName}" (brand icon itself is not announced).

steps.action: Press Space to select the focused card container.
steps.expectedResult: Card toggles to selected (aria-pressed=true) and shows selected indicator styling; no delete UI opens.

steps.action: Press Tab once to move focus to the delete button within the same card.
steps.expectedResult: Visible :focus-visible styling appears on the delete button; its accessible name is "Delete card ending in {last4}".

steps.action: Press Escape without activating delete.
steps.expectedResult: No confirmation dialog is shown (since it was not opened); focus remains on the delete button and no selection state changes.

steps.action: Activate the delete button with Enter to open confirmation.
steps.expectedResult: Inline anchored confirmation dialog/popover opens with prompt text that includes the same card identifier (ending in {last4}) and shows two actions: Cancel and Delete.

steps.action: Click outside the confirmation popover.
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation popover closes; focus returns to the delete button.

steps.action: Activate the delete button again to reopen confirmation, then choose "Delete".
steps.expectedResult: Deletion request starts; spinner replaces delete icon; both delete and card selection are disabled until completion.

steps.action: Wait for success and observe focus placement.
steps.expectedResult: Card is removed after collapse/fade; focus moves to the next card (or previous / list container fallback). Remaining cards keep correct focus order (card container first, then delete).

flows.completionCriteria: After an initial delete failure, the inline error message is shown and the user successfully retries deletion (with confirmation required again) resulting in card removal and correct post-delete focus placement.
flows.name: Delete fails (server error), show inline error, then retry

steps.action: Click the delete icon button on the payment card.
steps.expectedResult: Inline confirmation popover opens; delete does not trigger card selection.

steps.action: Click "Delete" in the confirmation popover.
steps.expectedResult: Async delete begins; spinner shows inside delete button; both delete and selection are disabled until the request completes.

steps.action: System returns a delete failure response (e.g., network/server error).
steps.expectedResult: Card remains visible; controls are re-enabled; an inline error message appears within payment_card below content: "Could not delete this card. Try again."

steps.action: Click the delete button again to retry deletion (confirmation required again).
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation popover opens again with Cancel/Delete; error message remains visible until a successful delete or until host clears it.

steps.action: Click "Delete" to submit retry, then wait for success.
steps.expectedResult: Spinner shows; on success the card collapses/fades and is removed; focus moves to next/previous card or list container if none remain; error message is no longer present because the card is removed.

    "Selection affordance is undefined (entire card vs radio/button), so keyboard interaction pattern and semantic role/aria-checked labeling are missing",

    "Focus management is undefined (visible focus ring on card and delete, focus order, and where focus goes after deletion)",
    "No guidance on preventing accidental activation when delete is inside a selectable card (keyboard and pointer event separation)",
    "Card brand icon alternative text/aria-hidden behavior is not specified (decorative vs informative)",
    "Text announced format is unspecified for masked number and expiry (e.g., reading out asterisks vs 'ending in 1234', 'expires 05/27')"
  ],
  "missingStates": [
    "Selected state visual styling for the active card (border/background/check indicator) is not defined",
    "Hover/pressed states for the card container and delete action are not defined",
    "Disabled/non-interactive state (e.g., cannot select or cannot delete) is not defined",
    "Delete confirmation state/workflow (confirm/cancel) is not defined for a destructive action",
    "Deleting in-progress/loading state is not defined (spinner, disabling controls, preventing double submit)",
    "Delete failure/error state is not defined (error message placement, retry behavior)",
    "Edge case state for expired card (expiry in past) is not defined (labeling/styling/warnings)",
    "Missing/unknown brand icon state is not defined (fallback icon/text)"
  ],
  "recommendations": [
    "Specify the selection UI pattern (radio-style list item vs clickable card button) and define required ARIA (role, aria-checked/selected) plus keyboard behavior (Enter/Space to select)",
    "Define destructive delete flow: inline confirmation (e.g., modal/popover) with confirm/cancel labels, and ensure delete is a distinct button to avoid triggering selection",
    "Add explicit interaction states: default/hover/active/focus/selected/disabled for both the card container and delete action, mapped to design tokens",
    "Define async behaviors for delete: disable delete while pending, show progress indicator, handle success removal animation, and show error with retry",
    "Provide screen-reader-friendly strings for masked number and expiry (e.g., 'Visa ending in 1234, expires 05/27, John Doe') and mark brand icon decorative if redundant",
    "Document focus rules: initial focus target, focus ring styling, and post-delete focus placement (next card, previous card, or list container)"
  ],

    "Layout behavior for narrow widths is unspecified (stacking order of brand icon, number, expiry, name, and delete action)",
    "Text overflow/truncation rules are missing for long cardholder names and small containers (ellipsis vs wrap, max lines)",
    "Placement of delete action on mobile is undefined (right-aligned, overflow menu, second row) and how it avoids accidental taps",
    "Minimum touch target sizes and spacing between selectable area and delete control are not specified for mobile",

accessibilityGaps: No semantic role specified for the selectable card (e.g., button vs radio option) and no keyboard interaction pattern defined (Enter/Space, roving tabindex if in a list)
No focus-visible styling requirements for the card container and the delete action
Delete action affordance not specified as icon-only or text; if icon-only, missing accessible name/aria-label requirements
Card brand icon missing alternative text/ARIA treatment (decorative vs meaningful) for screen readers
No guidance on preventing click/activation conflicts between selecting the card and activating delete (including keyboard/screen reader activation)
No announced status messaging defined for async delete (e.g., aria-live for success/failure)
missingStates: Selected state styling and behavior (how selection is indicated; whether selection is mutually exclusive in a list)
Hover/pressed/focus states for the card and delete action
Disabled state (e.g., when actions are not permitted or while delete is in progress)
Delete confirmation state (modal/popover) to prevent accidental destructive action
Deleting/in-progress state (spinner, label change, preventing selection while deleting)
Delete error state (failed deletion messaging and recovery action)
Empty/unknown data handling (missing expiry, cardholder name, or brand; placeholder vs hide field)
Long cardholder name overflow handling state (truncate/wrap) not defined
recommendations: Specify the selection model: treat each card as a button or a radio-like option within a list, and define keyboard behavior (Tab + Enter/Space; arrow-key navigation if radio/listbox pattern)
Define visual tokens/variants for default, hover, focus, pressed, and selected states (border/background change and checkmark or selected label)
Make delete a real button element with a clear accessible name (e.g., "Delete card ending in 1234") and ensure focus ring is visible
Add a confirmation step for deletion (dialog or popover) with clear primary/secondary actions and focus management
Define async deletion UX: disable interactions while deleting, show progress indicator, and provide inline error messaging on failure with retry
Define click-target rules: clicking card selects; clicking delete does not also select; stop propagation and ensure keyboard activation maps correctly
Clarify formatting rules for expiry (MM/YY vs MM/YYYY) and localization expectations; specify placeholder behavior when data is unavailable
Specify screen reader treatment for brand icon (decorative if redundant with text; otherwise provide text alternative like "Visa")
responsiveGaps: No layout rules for small widths (stacking order of brand icon, number, expiry, name, and delete action)
No truncation/wrapping behavior defined for long cardholder names and how it affects placement of expiry and delete
No minimum touch target sizes specified for the delete action and overall card on mobile
No guidance on where the delete action moves on narrow screens (top-right, inline, overflow menu) and how to avoid accidental taps
No constraints for multi-line wrapping vs fixed-height card (e.g., consistent heights in a list/grid) defined

coveredBehaviors: Payment card integrates child components to render brand icon, masked card number, expiry (MM/YY), and cardholder name with placeholders for missing data
Card selection uses radio semantics (role=radio, aria-checked) and triggers parent selection updates via on_select payloads (card_id), including keyboard activation (Space/Enter)
Delete action is an icon-only button with accessible name including last4; opening confirmation does not also select the card (event propagation boundary)

Delete confirmation dialog flow: open -> cancel (Escape/Cancel) restores focus and does not delete; open -> confirm triggers async delete state, disables selection + delete, and on success removes card
Delete failure recovery: failed async delete re-enables interactions, shows inline error with aria-live polite announcement, and supports retry leading to success and removal
coveredStates: focus-visible (keyboard focus on radio and delete button)
deleting/in-progress (selection and delete disabled; spinner/progress indicator)

decisions.decision: Implement selection using a radio-group pattern: each Payment Card renders a focusable element with role="radio" and aria-checked reflecting selected state; the parent list (outside this component) is expected to provide role="radiogroup" and manage roving tabindex so only the selected card is tabbable. Within the card: Space and Enter activate selection; arrow-key navigation is handled by the parent list, not by the card itself.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing semantic role and keyboard pattern in a way that matches the common “choose one saved payment method” model while keeping the card component reusable; delegating arrow-key roving tabindex to the parent is conservative because the list container is not part of the parsed components.
decisions.sourceGap: No semantic role specified for the selectable card (e.g., button vs radio option) and no keyboard interaction pattern defined (Enter/Space, roving tabindex if in a list)

decisions.decision: Selected state is indicated by a distinct border color and a 2px inset ring plus aria-checked="true"; no additional checkmark icon is added. Selection is mutually exclusive when used in a list, with only one card selected at a time (enforced by the parent).
decisions.rationale: Defines a concrete visual and ARIA indication for selection without introducing new components (e.g., a checkmark), and aligns with a conservative “single selected payment method” interaction model implied by selecting a saved card.
decisions.sourceGap: Selected state styling and behavior (how selection is indicated; whether selection is mutually exclusive in a list)

decisions.decision: Provide focus-visible styling for both the card and delete button: a 2px outline (or box-shadow ring) with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors, offset by 2px, shown only for keyboard focus (via :focus-visible).
decisions.rationale: Establishes explicit, testable focus treatment for keyboard users on both interactive surfaces, resolving the gap while remaining implementation-agnostic about exact token values.
decisions.sourceGap: No focus-visible styling requirements for the card container and the delete action

decisions.decision: Define interaction states: default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, selected. On hover, the card background subtly changes; on pressed, the card slightly darkens; the delete button has hover and pressed states independent of the card. These state styles must not change layout (no size shifts).
decisions.rationale: Adds the missing state definitions in a way that is consistent with standard UI behavior and prevents layout jank, making styling and snapshot tests deterministic.
decisions.sourceGap: Hover/pressed/focus states for the card and delete action

decisions.decision: Render the delete affordance as an icon-only <button type="button"> with an accessible name via aria-label in the form "Delete card ending in 1234" (using the last 4 digits). The visible icon is marked aria-hidden="true".
decisions.rationale: Resolves ambiguity about the affordance while ensuring screen reader users get a specific, disambiguating label; using the last 4 digits is conservative and relies only on already-displayed data.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete action affordance not specified as icon-only or text; if icon-only, missing accessible name/aria-label requirements

decisions.decision: Treat the card brand icon as decorative by default: render with aria-hidden="true" and empty alt (if using ). If brand text is not otherwise present, include visually-hidden text within payment_card like "Visa"/"Mastercard"/"American Express" derived from the brand value.
decisions.rationale: Avoids redundant announcements when the brand is conveyed elsewhere, while providing a fallback that preserves meaning without forcing new visible UI.
decisions.sourceGap: Card brand icon missing alternative text/ARIA treatment (decorative vs meaningful) for screen readers

decisions.decision: Clicking or keyboard-activating the delete button must not also select the card: the delete handler stops propagation and prevents default selection activation. Only activations originating on the card container (excluding the delete button subtree) trigger selection.
decisions.rationale: Provides an explicit, implementable rule to prevent conflicting activations across pointer and keyboard interactions, addressing a common nested-interactive control hazard.
decisions.sourceGap: No guidance on preventing click/activation conflicts between selecting the card and activating delete (including keyboard/screen reader activation)

decisions.decision: Require a confirmation dialog before deletion: activating delete opens a modal dialog with title "Delete payment method?" and body text including the last 4 digits; actions are "Cancel" (default focus) and "Delete" (destructive). Focus is trapped within the dialog, Escape closes to the delete button, and confirming triggers the async delete.
decisions.rationale: Defines a concrete confirmation state and focus management without introducing additional parsed subcomponents; this is conservative for destructive actions and unblocks implementation and testing of the delete flow.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete confirmation state (modal/popover) to prevent accidental destructive action

decisions.decision: During deletion (after confirmation): disable both selection and delete (aria-disabled="true" on the card radio, disabled on the delete button) and show an inline spinner in place of the delete icon. Prevent any state change until the request resolves.
decisions.rationale: Defines the missing in-progress and disabled behaviors in a minimal way that avoids race conditions and inconsistent UI while keeping the component deterministic.
decisions.sourceGap: Deleting/in-progress state (spinner, label change, preventing selection while deleting)

decisions.decision: Announce async delete results using an aria-live="polite" region within the Payment Card that emits: on success, "Card deleted"; on failure, "Delete failed. Try again." The live region is visually hidden and only present when a message is active.
decisions.rationale: Provides explicit status messaging for screen reader users without requiring global toast infrastructure; messages are short and testable.
decisions.sourceGap: No announced status messaging defined for async delete (e.g., aria-live for success/failure)

decisions.decision: On delete failure: keep the card visible and interactive again, render an inline error message beneath the card details, and keep the delete button available as a retry (same confirmation step applies).
decisions.rationale: Defines a concrete error state and recovery path while avoiding speculation about navigation or list-level removal; keeping the card prevents accidental data loss perceptions.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete error state (failed deletion messaging and recovery action)

decisions.decision: Display expiry in MM/YY format (e.g., 04/27). Do not localize the order or separator within this component; the input must be provided as month and two-digit year (or preformatted string matching MM/YY).
decisions.rationale: Resolves formatting ambiguity with a stable, compact format commonly used for card expiry and avoids introducing localization requirements not present in the brief.
decisions.sourceGap: Clarify formatting rules for expiry (MM/YY vs MM/YYYY) and localization expectations; specify placeholder behavior when data is unavailable

decisions.decision: If brand, expiry, or cardholder name is unavailable, render a placeholder em dash (—) in the corresponding field position; do not hide the field. Card number last-4 is required; if missing, render "****" as the last group.
decisions.rationale: Provides deterministic rendering and layout stability for missing data without inventing new copy; placeholders avoid shifting content and maintain consistent card structure.
decisions.sourceGap: Empty/unknown data handling (missing expiry, cardholder name, or brand; placeholder vs hide field)

decisions.decision: Cardholder name is single-line with truncation (CSS line-clamp/ellipsis) and a tooltip via title attribute containing the full name; it must not wrap to multiple lines.
decisions.rationale: Defines an explicit overflow behavior that preserves consistent card height and layout, addressing the missing overflow handling with minimal UI additions.
decisions.sourceGap: Long cardholder name overflow handling state (truncate/wrap) not defined

decisions.decision: At widths < 360px: layout stacks into two rows—row 1: brand icon + masked card number (left) and delete button (right); row 2: cardholder name (left) and expiry (right). At >= 360px keep a single-row layout with delete aligned to the far right.
decisions.rationale: Provides explicit small-width rules and element ordering without introducing an overflow menu, keeping interaction simple and predictable across breakpoints.
decisions.sourceGap: No layout rules for small widths (stacking order of brand icon, number, expiry, name, and delete action)

decisions.decision: Enforce minimum touch targets: delete button has a minimum interactive area of 44x44px; the overall card selection target is the full card container with at least 44px height.
decisions.rationale: Resolves missing mobile ergonomics requirements with widely accepted minimums, enabling consistent implementation and QA validation.
decisions.sourceGap: No minimum touch target sizes specified for the delete action and overall card on mobile

decisions.decision: Use a fixed two-row maximum layout with truncation (no multi-line wrapping) so all cards in a list have consistent height; content that would exceed the allotted space is truncated rather than expanding the card.
decisions.rationale: Addresses the missing constraint on multi-line wrapping vs fixed height in a conservative way that supports stable list/grid alignment.
decisions.sourceGap: No constraints for multi-line wrapping vs fixed-height card (e.g., consistent heights in a list/grid) defined

steps.action: Click on the payment card container (not on the delete button area) to select it.
steps.expectedResult: Card becomes selected: aria-checked="true" is set; selected border + 2px inset ring styling is applied; parent radiogroup updates so only one card is selected.

flows.completionCriteria: The payment card is selected via keyboard activation, reflected by aria-checked="true" and selected styling, with focus-visible ring shown on keyboard focus.

steps.action: Tab until the intended payment card receives focus (roving tabindex handled by parent radiogroup).
steps.expectedResult: Focused card shows :focus-visible ring (2px outline/ring with >=3:1 contrast, 2px offset); card has role="radio" and is focusable.

steps.action: Press Space (or Enter) to activate selection.
steps.expectedResult: Card becomes selected: aria-checked="true" updates; selected border + inset ring styling appears; only one card remains selected in the radiogroup.

flows.completionCriteria: The card is deleted after confirmation; the in-card aria-live region announces "Card deleted" and the card is removed from the saved payment methods list by the parent.
flows.name: Explore card details, then delete with confirmation

steps.action: Visually review the card details (brand, masked number, cardholder, expiry) including any placeholders.
steps.expectedResult: Masked card number is displayed (e.g., "**** **** **** 1234"); expiry is in MM/YY format; if brand/expiry/name missing, field shows an em dash (—); cardholder name is single-line truncated with ellipsis and has a title tooltip with full text.

steps.action: Hover the payment card container.
steps.expectedResult: Card hover styling applies (subtle background change) without layout shift.

steps.action: Hover the delete button.
steps.expectedResult: Delete button hover styling applies independently from the card; the button maintains minimum 44x44px hit area.

steps.action: Activate the delete icon button.
steps.expectedResult: A modal confirmation dialog opens with title "Delete payment method?" and body referencing the last 4 digits; focus is moved into the dialog with default focus on "Cancel"; activation does not select the card (event propagation is stopped).

steps.action: In the dialog, choose "Delete" to confirm.
steps.expectedResult: Async deletion starts: card selection is disabled (aria-disabled="true" on the card radio) and delete button is disabled; an inline spinner replaces the delete icon; no selection state changes occur while in progress.

steps.action: Wait for the delete request to resolve successfully.
steps.expectedResult: Card announces via its aria-live="polite" region: "Card deleted"; parent removes the card from the list UI (or otherwise reflects deletion) after success.

flows.completionCriteria: Deletion is canceled without selecting the card; focus returns to the delete button; then the card is successfully selected via keyboard.
flows.name: Open delete confirmation, cancel, then select card

steps.action: Tab to the delete icon button within a payment card.
steps.expectedResult: Delete button shows :focus-visible ring; accessible name is available (aria-label "Delete card ending in 1234"); the icon is aria-hidden="true".

steps.action: Press Enter/Space to activate delete.
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation dialog opens; focus is trapped inside the modal; default focus lands on "Cancel"; card is not selected as a side-effect.

steps.action: Activate "Cancel" (or press Escape).
steps.expectedResult: Dialog closes; focus returns to the delete button; no deletion occurs; card remains interactive.

steps.action: Shift focus to the card container (e.g., Shift+Tab once) and press Space to select.
steps.expectedResult: Card becomes selected with aria-checked="true" and selected styling; selection remains mutually exclusive within the parent radiogroup.

flows.completionCriteria: A delete attempt fails and shows inline error plus aria-live failure announcement; user can recover by retrying and completing deletion successfully.
flows.name: Delete fails (server error) and user retries

steps.action: Activate the delete icon button on a payment card.
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation dialog opens with Cancel (default focus) and Delete actions; delete activation does not select the card.

steps.action: Confirm deletion by activating "Delete" in the dialog.
steps.expectedResult: Async deletion starts: card selection is disabled (aria-disabled="true"), delete button is disabled, and spinner replaces delete icon until resolution.

steps.action: System receives a delete failure response (e.g., network/server error).
steps.expectedResult: Card remains visible; interactions are re-enabled; an inline error message appears beneath card details; aria-live announces "Delete failed. Try again."

steps.action: Activate delete again to retry (same card).
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation dialog opens again (confirmation is still required for retry); focus is trapped and Cancel is default focus.

steps.action: Confirm deletion again by activating "Delete".
steps.expectedResult: Async deletion starts again with the same in-progress disabled/spinner behavior; card cannot be selected during the request.

steps.action: Wait for the retry delete request to resolve successfully.
steps.expectedResult: aria-live announces "Card deleted"; parent removes the card from the list UI after success.

decisions.decision: Implement selection as a single-select radio pattern: the payment_card root renders with role="radio", aria-checked reflecting selected state, and is focusable with tabIndex=0 when enabled. Enter and Space on the focused payment_card trigger select_payment_card. If used outside a group, it still uses the same semantics but does not assume arrow-key navigation.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing keyboard interaction model and clarifies that the card is selectable as a mutually exclusive option, which is common for saved payment method selection. Using role="radio" with aria-checked provides clear assistive-tech semantics while keeping implementation conservative and testable without introducing additional components not in scope.
decisions.sourceGap: No defined keyboard interaction model for selecting the card (role, tab stop, Enter/Space behavior) versus activating the delete action

decisions.decision: Define tab order as two stops: (1) payment_card container (select), then (2) delete_card_action button. The delete action must be a native <button type="button"> (or equivalent) and must not be reachable by tab before the card container.
decisions.rationale: This explicitly separates selection from deletion in keyboard navigation, preventing accidental destructive activation and making interactions predictable. It also aligns with standard accessibility expectations and is straightforward to validate in tests.
decisions.sourceGap: No defined keyboard interaction model for selecting the card (role, tab stop, Enter/Space behavior) versus activating the delete action

decisions.decision: If delete is icon-only, set aria-label to "Delete card ending in {last4}". If a visible label is present, keep it as visible text and do not add redundant aria-label; instead, ensure the visible text is "Delete" and append visually-hidden context "card ending in {last4}" for screen readers.
decisions.rationale: This ensures the delete control has a unique, descriptive accessible name, particularly when multiple cards are listed. Using last4 is minimally identifying and avoids ambiguity while staying consistent with the masked display requirement.
decisions.sourceGap: No accessible name/aria-label guidance for the delete action, especially if it is icon-only

decisions.decision: Render the visible masked number as "•••• •••• •••• 1234" (or "**** **** **** 1234"), but provide an aria-label (or dedicated screen-reader-only text) for the number field as "Card ending in 1234" so assistive tech does not read each mask character.
decisions.rationale: This prevents verbose or confusing announcements of mask characters while still communicating the identifying last 4 digits. It is conservative because it does not expose the full PAN and uses a simple, consistent phrase for localization.
decisions.sourceGap: No screen-reader text strategy for masked card number (how to announce last 4 digits and avoid reading asterisks literally)

decisions.decision: Apply visible focus styling to both the payment_card container and the delete_card_action button using :focus-visible. The focus indicator must be at least a 2px outline (or ring) with a 2px offset from the component boundary and must not rely on color alone (e.g., include outline/ring, not only background change).
decisions.rationale: This directly resolves the lack of focus-visible requirements and provides an implementable, testable rule that works across themes. Using :focus-visible is conservative and avoids showing focus on mouse clicks while preserving keyboard accessibility.
decisions.sourceGap: No focus-visible styling requirements for card container and delete control

decisions.decision: Clicking or pressing Enter/Space on delete_card_action must not trigger select_payment_card. Implement by stopping event propagation from delete_card_action to payment_card and ensuring the delete button is not nested inside an element with implicit click-to-select behavior that captures activation (or handle onClick on the container with target checks).
decisions.rationale: This resolves activation conflicts between select and delete for both pointer and keyboard interactions. It is conservative because it does not require new UI patterns—only an explicit event contract and DOM structure discipline.
decisions.sourceGap: No guidance to prevent click/activation conflicts between selecting the card and clicking delete (e.g., stopPropagation) with accessible semantics

decisions.decision: Treat card_brand_icon as decorative when the brand is also provided as text to assistive tech elsewhere; otherwise, set accessible name on the icon as the brand value (e.g., "Visa"). Concretely: default to aria-hidden="true" for the icon and include brand in the payment_card accessible name/description string as "Visa card ending in 1234".
decisions.rationale: This avoids duplicate announcements while ensuring the brand is still conveyed when needed. Defaulting to decorative is conservative and reduces noise, while moving brand to a single accessible string improves consistency across icon asset variants.
decisions.sourceGap: No indication of how the card brand icon is announced (decorative vs labeled with brand name)

decisions.decision: When selected, payment_card must show a clear selected indicator: a 2px border in the primary accent color plus a subtle selected background tint. Additionally, expose selection via aria-checked="true" per the radio semantics.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing selected state and ensures both visual and non-visual users can determine the current selection. Border+tint is a minimal, common pattern that remains legible in dense lists.
decisions.sourceGap: Selected state styling/indicator for the currently selected card

decisions.decision: Define interactive states: payment_card hover increases elevation by one step (or applies a subtle hover background) and pressed applies a slight scale-down (e.g., 0.99) or darker background; delete_card_action hover applies a background wash and pressed applies a darker wash. These states must not be the only indicator of focus (focus-visible remains separate).
decisions.rationale: This fills in missing hover/pressed behavior with conservative, widely used affordances without needing exact token names. Separating focus from hover ensures accessibility and consistent behavior across input modes.
decisions.sourceGap: Hover/pressed states for the card container and delete action

decisions.decision: Support a disabled delete state: when deletion is not allowed, render delete_card_action as disabled (disabled attribute for <button>) with tooltip/title text "You don’t have permission to delete this card" and keep it focusable only if the product already uses focusable-disabled patterns; otherwise remove from tab order via native disabled behavior.
decisions.rationale: This addresses the missing disabled state with a default that is compatible with native controls and predictable for accessibility. Providing a short explanation via title/tooltip is a minimal addition that reduces confusion.
decisions.sourceGap: Disabled state for delete (e.g., insufficient permissions, locked payment method)

decisions.decision: Require confirmation before deletion using a modal dialog. Dialog copy: title "Delete payment method?" body "This will remove {brand} card ending in {last4} from your saved payment methods." Primary button "Delete" (destructive styling) and secondary "Cancel". On confirm, trigger delete_payment_card; on cancel, close dialog and return focus to delete_card_action.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing confirmation state with a standard, accessible pattern that reduces accidental destructive actions. It is conservative because it avoids inline popovers that can be harder to implement accessibly and ensures clear focus management.
decisions.sourceGap: Delete confirmation state (dialog/popover) to prevent accidental destructive action

decisions.decision: During deletion in progress, disable delete_card_action and replace its icon/label with a small inline spinner while preserving the button width. Also set aria-busy="true" on payment_card to signal the busy state to assistive tech.
decisions.rationale: This defines a concrete loading behavior that prevents duplicate submissions and provides clear feedback. Using aria-busy on the card is a minimal accessibility improvement without introducing new announcement systems.
decisions.sourceGap: Deletion in-progress state (loading/spinner, delete button disabled)

decisions.decision: On deletion failure, keep the card visible, re-enable delete_card_action, and show an inline error message within payment_card: "Couldn’t delete this payment method. Try again." Provide a "Retry" affordance that triggers delete_payment_card again and ensure the error region has role="alert".
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing error state with a local, testable feedback mechanism that does not depend on global toast infrastructure. role="alert" ensures the failure is announced without extra complexity.
decisions.sourceGap: Deletion error state (failure feedback and retry behavior)

decisions.decision: Cardholder name must be single-line with end ellipsis and a title attribute containing the full name. Masked number and expiry remain single-line and must not wrap. If localization causes label expansion, the details section truncates with ellipsis rather than wrapping.
decisions.rationale: This resolves long-text overflow behavior with a conservative rule that preserves row height consistency in lists. The title attribute provides a minimal way to access full content without introducing additional UI.
decisions.sourceGap: Long-text overflow state for cardholder name and localized labels

decisions.decision: If card_brand is unknown/unsupported, render a generic card icon asset and set the brand text used in accessible strings to "Card" (e.g., "Card ending in 1234"). Do not omit the icon slot to avoid layout shifts.
decisions.rationale: This addresses the fallback state while keeping layout stable and avoiding missing content. Using a generic label is conservative and avoids incorrect brand announcements.
decisions.sourceGap: Unknown/unsupported card brand fallback state (generic icon or text)

decisions.decision: For narrow containers (<360px), keep a single-row layout: brand icon left, details in the middle, delete action right. Details area truncates (no wrapping) and the delete action remains pinned to the right. If space becomes insufficient, cardholder name is the first field to truncate, then masked number; expiry remains visible.
decisions.rationale: This resolves responsive layout ambiguity without introducing a second layout mode that could increase complexity. Prioritizing expiry visibility is a conservative, user-relevant choice for identifying a payment method.
decisions.sourceGap: No layout rules for small widths: whether details stack (number/expiry/name) or truncate, and where the delete action moves

decisions.decision: Ensure delete_card_action has a minimum hit area of 44x44 px (via padding or an invisible hit target) even when the visible icon is smaller, and keep at least 8px spacing between the delete target and the card edge.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the missing touch target guidance with an established minimum that improves mobile usability. It is conservative because it does not require visible size changes, only hit area guarantees.
decisions.sourceGap: No guidance on minimum touch target sizes and spacing for the delete action in compact layouts

decisions.decision: Card brand icon uses a fixed size of 24x24 px on all breakpoints and remains vertically centered relative to the card content. It must not be hidden on small screens.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the lack of icon scaling/reflow rules with a simple fixed-size decision that prevents layout instability and preserves brand recognition without additional responsive complexity.
decisions.sourceGap: No definition of how the card brand icon scales or reflows on small screens (fixed size, alignment, or hidden)

decisions.decision: In lists, payment_card stretches to full available width of its container. Vertical spacing between adjacent cards is 12px in regular density and 8px in dense mode; dense mode is enabled by a boolean prop on payment_card (e.g., dense=true). Grid layout is not supported by this component itself; grid behavior is handled by the parent layout.
decisions.rationale: This resolves dense list behavior without inventing a new layout component. Constraining grid responsibility to the parent is conservative and keeps payment_card reusable and predictable.
decisions.sourceGap: No handling for dense lists: spacing between cards, whether the card stretches full-width, and how multiple cards behave in grid vs column layouts

coveredBehaviors: Renders a brand-specific icon for recognized brands (visa/mastercard/amex)
Falls back to a generic/unknown icon when brand is "unknown" or unsupported
Defaults to aria-hidden=true (decorative icon behavior) when aria_hidden is not provided
When aria_hidden=false and aria_label is provided, exposes an accessible name for the icon
Accepts size_px and applies it to the rendered icon dimensions; defaults to 24px when omitted
Renders masked card number text as provided
Applies accessible labeling for masked card number: defaults to "Card ending in {last4}"
Allows overriding masked number accessible label via masked_number_aria_label
Renders expiry date and cardholder name
When enable_overflow_rules is true, sets title attribute on cardholder name to the full name (for truncated display expectation)
Does not apply cardholder title attribute when enable_overflow_rules is false/undefined
Renders a native button with an accessible name including last4 ("Delete card ending in {last4}")
When can_delete=false, button is disabled, shows disabled_reason as title/tooltip, and does not invoke on_request_delete
When can_delete=true, clicking the button invokes on_request_delete with payment_method_id, last4, and card_brand
When is_deleting=true, button is disabled to prevent interactions (request/confirm/cancel)
Stops click event propagation to prevent parent card selection when delete is activated
Renders with radio selection semantics: role="radio" and aria-checked reflects selected prop
When selectable (default), card container is focusable (tabIndex=0) and invokes on_select with payment_method_id on click
Keyboard selection: Enter and Space on the focused card invoke on_select with payment_method_id
When selectable=false, card is not focusable and does not invoke on_select on click or keyboard activation
Passes masked number, last4, expiry (MM/YY formatting from month/year inputs), and cardholder_name to CardDetails
Renders CardBrandIcon with brand prop and aria-hidden by default (decorative)
Sets aria-busy="true" on the card container when deleting=true
Shows inline delete error message with role="alert" when delete_error_message is set
Wires delete flow: when DeleteCardAction confirms deletion or retry is triggered, invokes on_delete with payment_method_id
Prevents event collision: clicking delete action does not trigger on_select (stopPropagation contract)
Disables delete action when delete_enabled=false and forwards disabled reason/title

flows.completionCriteria: Target payment_card is selected (aria-checked="true") and visually indicated as selected; no deletion UI is triggered.
flows.name: Select a saved card (pointer)

steps.action: Click the payment card container to select it.
steps.expectedResult: select_payment_card fires; payment_card updates to selected styling (2px accent border + subtle tint) and sets aria-checked="true". Any previously selected card becomes aria-checked="false".

flows.completionCriteria: Card is removed from the list after a confirmed delete; delete confirmation dialog is closed.
flows.name: Delete a saved card (confirm, success)

steps.action: Activate the delete control on a payment card.
steps.expectedResult: A confirmation modal opens with title "Delete payment method?" and body including the card descriptor "{brand} card ending in {last4}". Focus moves into the dialog. The delete activation does not select the card.

steps.action: Confirm deletion by activating the dialog primary "Delete" action.
steps.expectedResult: delete_payment_card triggers. delete_card_action becomes disabled and shows an inline spinner while preserving width; payment_card sets aria-busy="true" until completion.

steps.action: Wait for the deletion request to complete successfully.
steps.expectedResult: The confirmation modal closes and the card is removed from the UI list. Focus moves to the next logical element in the list (e.g., next payment_card) handled by the parent page.

flows.completionCriteria: User successfully selects the intended card using keyboard; selection is communicated via aria-checked and visual selected styling.
flows.name: Explore details, tab stops, and responsive truncation; then select (keyboard)

steps.action: Tab to focus the payment card container.
steps.expectedResult: payment_card receives :focus-visible ring (2px outline with 2px offset). It is focusable and exposes role="radio" with aria-checked reflecting current selection state.

steps.action: Pause to review the card details and brand identification via assistive tech.
steps.expectedResult: Masked number is announced as "Card ending in {last4}" (not reading mask characters). Brand is conveyed via the payment_card accessible string (e.g., "Visa card ending in {last4}") while the card_brand_icon remains aria-hidden.

steps.action: Resize to a narrow container (e.g., <360px) or view in a narrow panel.
steps.expectedResult: Single-row layout remains: card_brand_icon left (fixed 24x24), details truncate without wrapping, delete action stays pinned right. Truncation priority applies: cardholder name truncates first, then masked number; expiry remains visible.

steps.action: Tab to focus the delete control (second tab stop) without activating it.
steps.expectedResult: delete_card_action receives :focus-visible ring. Accessible name is unique (e.g., aria-label "Delete card ending in {last4}" for icon-only).

steps.action: Shift+Tab back to the payment card container and activate selection with Space.
steps.expectedResult: select_payment_card fires. payment_card updates to selected styling and aria-checked="true" (radio semantics).

flows.completionCriteria: Delete action is not performed; user receives an explanation that deletion is not permitted and can continue interacting with the card.
flows.name: Attempt to delete when delete is disabled (permission/locked)

steps.action: Navigate to a card where deletion is not allowed and attempt to activate delete.
steps.expectedResult: delete_card_action is disabled (native disabled behavior). Activation does nothing; deletion confirmation modal does not open. A tooltip/title is available: "You don’t have permission to delete this card".

steps.action: Select the card instead using the payment card container.
steps.expectedResult: select_payment_card fires; payment_card becomes selected (aria-checked="true" + selected styling).

flows.completionCriteria: After a deletion failure, an inline error (role="alert") is shown; user can retry and deletion succeeds, removing the card.
flows.name: Delete fails; show inline error and recover via Retry

steps.action: Activate the delete control on a payment card.
steps.expectedResult: Confirmation modal opens; focus moves into the dialog. Delete activation does not select the card (event propagation prevented).

steps.action: Confirm deletion in the modal.
steps.expectedResult: delete_payment_card triggers; delete_card_action becomes disabled with spinner; payment_card sets aria-busy="true".

steps.action: Deletion request returns an error.
steps.expectedResult: Card remains visible. aria-busy is removed. delete_card_action is re-enabled. An inline error message appears within payment_card: "Couldn’t delete this payment method. Try again." and is announced via role="alert".

steps.action: Activate the inline "Retry" affordance.
steps.expectedResult: delete_payment_card triggers again. delete_card_action disables and shows spinner; payment_card sets aria-busy="true".

steps.action: Retry request completes successfully.
steps.expectedResult: Card is removed from the UI list; any inline error is cleared as the component unmounts/removes. Focus moves to the next logical element in the list handled by the parent page.

contractCompatibilityIssues: payment_card: does not emit/forward the delete_card_action contract callbacks; it passes on_request_delete as a no-op and does not provide any mechanism to open/drive the required confirmation dialog state from within component props.

delete_card_action: interface includes on_confirm_delete/on_cancel_delete/on_retry_delete but the implementation never invokes them; only on_request_delete is used. This is a concrete mismatch with the declared component interface returns and expected workflow responsibilities.
issuesFound: Confirmation flow is not implemented in generated components despite confirming being a required/covered canonical state in deterministicSummary; delete_card_action never opens or renders a confirmation dialog and never calls on_confirm_delete/on_cancel_delete.

payment_card passes a no-op on_request_delete to delete_card_action, preventing parent integration via the documented callback contract (parent cannot open confirmation modal based on component events).

component.business_context: Merchant dashboard UI for displaying and managing saved payment methods.
component.name: Payment Card

constraints: Card number must be displayed masked (e.g., **** **** **** 1234).

accessibility_gaps: No defined keyboard interaction model for selecting the card (role, tab stop, Enter/Space behavior) versus activating the delete action
No accessible name/aria-label guidance for the delete action, especially if it is icon-only
No screen-reader text strategy for masked card number (how to announce last 4 digits and avoid reading asterisks literally)
No focus-visible styling requirements for card container and delete control
No guidance to prevent click/activation conflicts between selecting the card and clicking delete (e.g., stopPropagation) with accessible semantics
No indication of how the card brand icon is announced (decorative vs labeled with brand name)
missing_states: Selected state styling/indicator for the currently selected card
Hover/pressed states for the card container and delete action
Disabled state for delete (e.g., insufficient permissions, locked payment method)
Delete confirmation state (dialog/popover) to prevent accidental destructive action
Deletion in-progress state (loading/spinner, delete button disabled)
Deletion error state (failure feedback and retry behavior)
Long-text overflow state for cardholder name and localized labels
Unknown/unsupported card brand fallback state (generic icon or text)
recommendations: Define selection UX: whether the whole card is a button/radio option, how selection is indicated (checkmark, border, background), and whether selection is single-select within a list
Specify destructive-action flow: confirmation pattern (modal vs inline), copy, and what happens on confirm/cancel, plus toast/inline feedback on success/failure
Add an explicit interaction contract to avoid event collisions: clicking delete must not also select the card; define pointer and keyboard behavior
Provide accessibility specs: roles/ARIA (e.g., button/radio), tab order (card then delete), Enter/Space activation, focus ring tokens, and aria-labels like "Delete card ending in 1234"
Define content formatting rules: expiry format validation (MM/YY), handling missing/unknown cardholder name, and localization expectations for separators and spacing
Define brand icon mapping and fallback behavior, including whether the icon is decorative and how brand text is exposed to assistive tech
Document token usage at a more concrete level (which text is primary/secondary, icon size, padding values, elevation on hover) to enable consistent implementation
responsive_gaps: No layout rules for small widths: whether details stack (number/expiry/name) or truncate, and where the delete action moves
No truncation/wrapping specification for long cardholder names and narrow containers (ellipsis vs multi-line)
No guidance on minimum touch target sizes and spacing for the delete action in compact layouts
No definition of how the card brand icon scales or reflows on small screens (fixed size, alignment, or hidden)
No handling for dense lists: spacing between cards, whether the card stretches full-width, and how multiple cards behave in grid vs column layouts

issues_found: Confirmation flow is not implemented in generated components despite confirming being a required/covered canonical state in deterministicSummary; delete_card_action never opens or renders a confirmation dialog and never calls on_confirm_delete/on_cancel_delete.

payment_card passes a no-op on_request_delete to delete_card_action, preventing parent integration via the documented callback contract (parent cannot open confirmation modal based on component events).

Radio-card pattern is implemented with role="radio" and aria-checked, but lacks required group semantics when used in a list (no role="radiogroup" provided by component; acceptable if parent supplies it, but not guaranteed).

recommendations: Specify the personal info fields, required/optional rules, and validation schema per field so Next gating and error rendering can be implemented

decisions.decision: Implement the step indicator as an ordered list (<ol>) with each step as a list item containing a <button type="button">. Apply aria-current="step" to the active step button, and set aria-disabled="true" on future step buttons (while still rendering them). The list has aria-label="KYC steps".
decisions.rationale: Defines concrete screen-reader semantics for steps and the active step, and conservatively avoids overpromising navigation by disabling future steps by default while still conveying progress.
decisions.sourceGap: Step indicator semantics not defined (aria-current for active step, progress/step list labeling for screen readers)

decisions.decision: Allow clicking step indicator buttons to navigate only to already-completed steps and the current step; disallow jumping forward. Completion is defined as having successfully advanced past a step at least once in the current session.
decisions.rationale: Resolves ambiguity about whether step indicator is interactive while keeping a conservative KYC flow that prevents skipping required steps.
decisions.sourceGap: Define wizard navigation rules (can users click step indicator to jump steps, can they skip steps, behavior when moving back after uploading files)

decisions.decision: Default initial state is step 1 (personal info) with no restoration of prior progress. Back button is rendered but disabled on step 1 (disabled attribute and aria-disabled="true").
decisions.rationale: Unblocks deterministic initialization and first-step navigation behavior without introducing persistence requirements that are not specified.
decisions.sourceGap: Initial wizard state not defined (which step is default, whether prior saved progress is restored)

decisions.decision: Implement minimal Next-gating on the personal info step: Next is enabled only when all fields in that step are valid; since fields are unspecified, implement the step as a required confirmation checkbox labeled "I confirm the above information is correct" and require it checked to proceed.
decisions.rationale: Creates an explicit, testable validation rule without inventing a full personal-info schema that is not present in the brief, while still enforcing a required action before progressing.
decisions.sourceGap: Per-step form validation states not defined (required fields, format errors, blocking Next until valid)

decisions.decision: When Next triggers an async action (document upload submission or selfie submission), set Next to loading and disabled (disabled attribute + aria-busy="true" on the step container); Back is also disabled during this period to prevent step changes mid-submit.
decisions.rationale: Defines concrete disabled/loading behavior to prevent double submits and inconsistent wizard state during asynchronous operations.
decisions.sourceGap: Next button disabled/loading state during uploads/submission not defined

decisions.decision: Document upload accepts multiple files with a max count of 3. Validate each file client-side: type must be application/pdf, image/jpeg, or image/png; size must be <= 10MB. Duplicates are detected by (name, size, lastModified) and rejected with an error. Invalid files are not added to the selected list.
decisions.rationale: Resolves multiple missing file-handling edge cases (count, duplicates, type/size validation) using conservative caps and deterministic duplicate detection suitable for tests.
decisions.sourceGap: File validation error states not defined (unsupported type, >10MB, multiple files allowed or not, duplicate file handling)

decisions.decision: Document upload maintains explicit UI states: empty (no files), selected (files listed), uploading (per-file progress indicator shown as indeterminate unless actual progress is available), success (file marked uploaded), failure (file marked failed with retry action), and removed (file removed from list). Uploads start immediately upon selection/drop (auto-upload).
decisions.rationale: Defines the missing upload lifecycle and whether uploads are immediate, enabling consistent UI generation and state-driven tests.
decisions.sourceGap: Document upload states not defined (empty/no file selected, uploading progress, upload success, upload failure, file removed)

decisions.decision: Dropzone supports drag states: idle, drag-over-accept, drag-over-reject. When dragging files over the dropzone, compute accept/reject based on the same type/size rules; apply a visible style change and announce "Files will be added" vs "Some files are not supported" via an aria-live="polite" region. On drop with rejected files, keep accepted files and show an inline error summary for rejected ones.
decisions.rationale: Specifies hover/active/reject behavior and feedback for invalid drops while keeping acceptance rules consistent with picker validation.
decisions.sourceGap: Drag-and-drop hover/active/reject states not defined (drag over highlight, dropping invalid file feedback)

decisions.decision: Make the dropzone focusable (tabIndex=0) and treat Enter/Space as opening the file picker. Also render a visible "Choose files" button inside the dropzone that triggers the same input. Do not require drag-and-drop for completion.
decisions.rationale: Provides a keyboard-accessible path for file selection and defines exact key behavior, satisfying accessibility without changing core functionality.
decisions.sourceGap: Keyboard interaction for drag-and-drop upload not specified (keyboard-accessible upload trigger, Enter/Space behavior on dropzone)

decisions.decision: Add a static instruction text element for each upload area and reference it with aria-describedby on the file input and dropzone. Document upload instruction text must include: "Accepted formats: PDF, JPG, PNG. Max size: 10MB. Up to 3 files."
decisions.rationale: Defines accessible names/instructions and ensures constraints are communicated consistently to assistive technologies.
decisions.sourceGap: File upload and selfie upload accessible names/instructions not specified (label text, accepted formats, max size communicated via aria-describedby)

decisions.decision: For field/file errors: set aria-invalid="true" on the invalid input/control and include the error message id in aria-describedby (appending to any existing described-by). Additionally, provide a step-level aria-live="assertive" error region that announces the first blocking error when Next is pressed and validation fails.
decisions.rationale: Defines explicit linking between errors and controls and provides deterministic announcement behavior for validation and upload failures.
decisions.sourceGap: Error messaging accessibility not specified (inline errors linked to fields/files with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, live region for upload errors)

decisions.decision: On successful Next/Back step transition, move focus to the step heading (an <h2> with tabIndex="-1"). On failed validation, move focus to the first invalid control in the current step; if none is focusable, focus the step-level error region.
decisions.rationale: Removes ambiguity about focus behavior, supports keyboard users, and enables predictable automated accessibility testing.
decisions.sourceGap: Focus management between steps not specified (where focus lands after Next/Back, preserving focus on validation errors)

decisions.decision: Implement selfie step as a single image file upload (JPG/PNG only, max 10MB) with preview and actions: Replace (opens picker) and Remove (clears selection). Do not implement camera capture in this version.
decisions.rationale: Resolves ambiguity about upload vs capture with the simplest implementation that aligns with the existing file-upload pattern and avoids additional device permission complexity.
decisions.sourceGap: Selfie step upload/capture states not defined (whether it is file upload vs camera capture, preview, retake/remove)

decisions.decision: When entering the final status view, fetch status asynchronously and show a loading state (skeleton/text "Loading status..."). On fetch error, show "Unable to load status" with a Retry button that re-fetches. If status is not one of pending_review/approved/rejected, render "Status unavailable".
decisions.rationale: Defines the missing retrieval states and ensures the UI handles unknown backend responses safely.
decisions.sourceGap: Verification status retrieval states not defined (loading status, retry on fetch error, unknown/unavailable status)

decisions.decision: Each status renders an icon plus text, not color alone: pending shows a clock icon and "Pending review"; approved shows a check icon and "Approved"; rejected shows an alert icon and "Rejected". Color is supplemental only.
decisions.rationale: Ensures status meaning is conveyed without relying on color, addressing color-blind and contrast scenarios conservatively.
decisions.sourceGap: Verification status relies on color mapping without non-color cues specified (icons/text patterns to meet color-contrast and color-blind needs)

decisions.decision: Wizard container max-width is 720px with 16px padding on mobile and 24px on >=768px; center aligned. Step indicator: on <360px, render condensed variant "1/3", "2/3", "3/3" with the current step name below; on >=360px, render horizontal steps and allow label wrapping to 2 lines with ellipsis after 2 lines. Navigation: on mobile, render a sticky bottom bar with Back and Next full-width stacked (Next above Back); on >=768px, render inline with Back left and Next right. Dropzone minimum height is 120px and instruction text wraps; tap targets (buttons) minimum height 44px.
decisions.rationale: Resolves multiple responsive ambiguities (container, step indicator, button placement, dropzone sizing, truncation) with clear breakpoints and deterministic behavior.
decisions.sourceGap: Overall wizard container constraints not defined (max width, padding, and how it behaves in embedded vs full-page contexts)
