flows.name: Complete KYC wizard (direct path) and reach Pending review status

steps.action: Open the KYC wizard and land on step 1 (Personal info).
steps.expectedResult: Step indicator shows Personal info as active (aria-current="step"); Back is disabled; focus is on the step heading (<h2> with tabIndex="-1").

steps.action: Check the required confirmation checkbox in Personal info step.
steps.expectedResult: Personal info step is considered valid; Next becomes enabled.
steps.inputData: I confirm the above information is correct = checked

steps.action: Click Next to proceed to Document upload.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard advances to step 2; step heading receives focus; step indicator marks step 2 as active and step 1 as completed (clickable per rules).

steps.action: Select one valid document file using the file picker from the document upload control.
steps.expectedResult: Selected file is added and auto-upload starts; file shows uploading then success state when complete.

steps.action: Click Next to proceed to Selfie step after document upload is complete.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard advances to step 3; step heading receives focus; step indicator marks step 3 as active.

steps.action: Upload a valid selfie image file (JPG/PNG).
steps.expectedResult: Selfie shows a preview and is considered valid for submission.

steps.action: Click Next to submit selfie and enter verification status view.
steps.expectedResult: Next enters loading/disabled state; Back is disabled; step container is aria-busy="true" during async submit; on success, status view renders and begins fetching status.

steps.action: Wait for verification status fetch to complete.
steps.expectedResult: Loading state "Loading status..." is replaced by Pending review status with icon + text (not color-only).

flows.completionCriteria: User successfully completes the wizard after navigating back and using the step indicator to revisit completed steps, ending on an Approved status display.
flows.name: Explore steps, go back, use step indicator for completed steps, and finish KYC

steps.action: Open the KYC wizard on a small screen (<360px width).
steps.expectedResult: Step indicator uses condensed display (e.g., "1/3") with current step name shown below; sticky mobile navigation shows Next above Back (both full-width) with Back disabled on step 1.

steps.action: Attempt to click the step indicator for step 2 (Document upload) while on step 1.
steps.expectedResult: Step 2 button is aria-disabled="true" and does not navigate; user remains on Personal info step.

steps.action: Check the confirmation checkbox on step 1 and click Next.
steps.expectedResult: Moves to step 2; focus lands on step 2 heading; step 1 is now considered completed and becomes navigable via step indicator.

steps.action: Drag-and-drop two valid files onto the dropzone.
steps.expectedResult: Dropzone enters drag-over-accept state and announces via aria-live polite; both files are added; auto-upload starts; each file transitions to success state when complete.

steps.action: Click Back to return to Personal info.
steps.expectedResult: Returns to step 1; focus moves to step 1 heading; previously completed state is retained for step 1.

steps.action: Click the step indicator button for Document upload (step 2).
steps.expectedResult: Navigates to step 2 because it is completed; focus moves to step 2 heading; uploaded files remain listed with their upload success states.

steps.action: Use the document upload control to remove one of the previously uploaded files.
steps.expectedResult: Removed file disappears from the list; remaining uploaded file stays; step remains valid if at least one document remains uploaded.

steps.action: Click Next to go to Selfie step.
steps.expectedResult: Moves to step 3; focus lands on step 3 heading.

steps.action: Upload a selfie image, then choose Replace to select a different selfie.
steps.expectedResult: First image preview appears; Replace opens picker and swaps to new preview; selection remains valid after replacement.

steps.action: Click Next to submit and enter verification status view.
steps.expectedResult: Next shows loading/disabled and Back is disabled during async submit; status view loads and fetches status with "Loading status...".

steps.action: Observe status fetch returning Approved.
steps.expectedResult: Approved status renders with check icon + "Approved" text; color is supplemental only.

flows.completionCriteria: User encounters validation errors due to invalid document files, cannot proceed until fixed, then successfully reaches the verification status view.
flows.name: Invalid document upload (type/size/duplicate/max count) blocks Next; user fixes and continues

steps.action: Open wizard and complete step 1 by checking the confirmation checkbox, then click Next.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard advances to Document upload (step 2) and focuses the step heading.

steps.action: Attempt to drop a mix of valid and invalid files onto the dropzone.
steps.expectedResult: Dropzone enters drag-over-reject if any file is invalid and announces "Some files are not supported" via aria-live polite; on drop, accepted files are added and rejected files are not added; inline error summary lists rejected reasons (unsupported type and/or too large).
steps.inputData: valid: id.png (<=10MB); invalid: statement.docx; invalid: large_scan.pdf (>10MB)

steps.action: Try to add a duplicate of an already selected file via file picker.
steps.expectedResult: Duplicate is rejected (matched by name/size/lastModified); error is shown and announced; duplicate is not added to the list.

steps.action: Try to exceed the max document file count by adding additional valid files beyond the limit.
steps.expectedResult: Only up to 3 files are kept; additional files are rejected with an inline error indicating max 3 files; rejected ones are not added.
steps.inputData: add 3 more valid images to exceed total >3

steps.action: Click Next while document step is still blocking due to missing required uploaded documents (e.g., none successfully uploaded yet or all removed/failed).
steps.expectedResult: Wizard does not advance; step-level aria-live assertive region announces the first blocking error; focus moves to the first invalid control (upload dropzone or file input) and it is marked aria-invalid="true" with aria-describedby including the error message id.

steps.action: Use the keyboard to focus the dropzone and press Enter to open the file picker, then select one valid PDF.
steps.expectedResult: File picker opens from Enter key; selected file is added; auto-upload starts; file transitions to success state; any previous blocking error clears once requirements are met.
steps.inputData: tab to dropzone, Enter; select passport.pdf (<=10MB, application/pdf)

steps.action: Click Next to proceed to Selfie step once at least one document is successfully uploaded.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard advances to Selfie step (step 3) and focuses the step heading.

steps.action: Upload a valid selfie image and click Next to submit.
steps.expectedResult: Async submit disables Back and shows Next loading; on success, status view loads and begins status fetch.

steps.action: Status fetch fails once; user clicks Retry.
steps.expectedResult: UI shows "Unable to load status" and a Retry button; clicking Retry re-fetches and shows loading state again.

steps.action: Status fetch returns an unknown status value.
steps.expectedResult: UI renders "Status unavailable" (safe fallback) rather than pending/approved/rejected.

steps.outputJson: {"decisions":[{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","kyc_step_indicator"],"code":"step_indicator_semantics","decision":"Implement the step indicator as an ordered list (<ol>) with each step as a list item containing a <button type=\"button\">. Apply aria-current=\"step\" to the active step button, and set aria-disabled=\"true\" on future step buttons (while still rendering them). The list has aria-label=\"KYC steps\".","rationale":"Defines concrete screen-reader semantics for steps and the active step, and conservatively avoids overpromising navigation by disabling future steps by default while still conveying progress.","sourceGap":"Step indicator semantics not defined (aria-current for active step, progress/step list labeling for screen readers)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","kyc_step_indicator"],"code":"step_click_navigation_rules","decision":"Allow clicking step indicator buttons to navigate only to already-completed steps and the current step; disallow jumping forward. Completion is defined as having successfully advanced past a step at least once in the current session.","rationale":"Resolves ambiguity about whether step indicator is interactive while keeping a conservative KYC flow that prevents skipping required steps.","sourceGap":"Define wizard navigation rules (can users click step indicator to jump steps, can they skip steps, behavior when moving back after uploading files)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","personal_info_step","document_upload_step","selfie_step","wizard_navigation","back_button","next_button"],"code":"wizard_initial_state_and_back_button","decision":"Default initial state is step 1 (personal info) with no restoration of prior progress. Back button is rendered but disabled on step 1 (disabled attribute and aria-disabled=\"true\").","rationale":"Unblocks deterministic initialization and first-step navigation behavior without introducing persistence requirements that are not specified.","sourceGap":"Initial wizard state not defined (which step is default, whether prior saved progress is restored)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","wizard_navigation","next_button","personal_info_step"],"code":"personal_info_min_validation","decision":"Implement minimal Next-gating on the personal info step: Next is enabled only when all fields in that step are valid; since fields are unspecified, implement the step as a required confirmation checkbox labeled \"I confirm the above information is correct\" and require it checked to proceed.","rationale":"Creates an explicit, testable validation rule without inventing a full personal-info schema that is not present in the brief, while still enforcing a required action before progressing.","sourceGap":"Per-step form validation states not defined (required fields, format errors, blocking Next until valid)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","wizard_navigation","next_button","document_upload","document_upload_step","selfie_step"],"code":"async_next_loading_and_disable","decision":"When Next triggers an async action (document upload submission or selfie submission), set Next to loading and disabled (disabled attribute + aria-busy=\"true\" on the step container); Back is also disabled during this period to prevent step changes mid-submit.","rationale":"Defines concrete disabled/loading behavior to prevent double submits and inconsistent wizard state during asynchronous operations.","sourceGap":"Next button disabled/loading state during uploads/submission not defined"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["document_upload"],"code":"document_upload_file_rules","decision":"Document upload accepts multiple files with a max count of 3. Validate each file client-side: type must be application/pdf, image/jpeg, or image/png; size must be <= 10MB. Duplicates are detected by (name, size, lastModified) and rejected with an error. Invalid files are not added to the selected list.","rationale":"Resolves multiple missing file-handling edge cases (count, duplicates, type/size validation) using conservative caps and deterministic duplicate detection suitable for tests.","sourceGap":"File validation error states not defined (unsupported type, >10MB, multiple files allowed or not, duplicate file handling)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["document_upload"],"code":"document_upload_states_and_progress","decision":"Document upload maintains explicit UI states: empty (no files), selected (files listed), uploading (per-file progress indicator shown as indeterminate unless actual progress is available), success (file marked uploaded), failure (file marked failed with retry action), and removed (file removed from list). Uploads start immediately upon selection/drop (auto-upload).","rationale":"Defines the missing upload lifecycle and whether uploads are immediate, enabling consistent UI generation and state-driven tests.","sourceGap":"Document upload states not defined (empty/no file selected, uploading progress, upload success, upload failure, file removed)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["document_upload"],"code":"drag_drop_active_reject_states","decision":"Dropzone supports drag states: idle, drag-over-accept, drag-over-reject. When dragging files over the dropzone, compute accept/reject based on the same type/size rules; apply a visible style change and announce \"Files will be added\" vs \"Some files are not supported\" via an aria-live=\"polite\" region. On drop with rejected files, keep accepted files and show an inline error summary for rejected ones.","rationale":"Specifies hover/active/reject behavior and feedback for invalid drops while keeping acceptance rules consistent with picker validation.","sourceGap":"Drag-and-drop hover/active/reject states not defined (drag over highlight, dropping invalid file feedback)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["document_upload"],"code":"dropzone_keyboard_support","decision":"Make the dropzone focusable (tabIndex=0) and treat Enter/Space as opening the file picker. Color is supplemental only.","rationale":"Ensures status meaning is conveyed without relying on color, addressing color-blind and contrast scenarios conservatively.","sourceGap":"Verification status relies on color mapping without non-color cues specified (icons/text patterns to meet color-contrast and color-blind needs)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["kyc_verification_wizard","kyc_step_indicator","wizard_navigation","document_upload"],"code":"responsive_layout_rules","decision":"Wizard container max-width is 720px with 16px padding on mobile and 24px on >=768px; center aligned. decisions.decision: Implement the step indicator as an ordered list (<ol>) inside a <nav aria-label="KYC steps">. Each step label is rendered as plain text (non-interactive). The current step item sets aria-current="step" and includes visually rendered helper text "Step X of 3". Additionally, the wizard renders a dedicated aria-live="polite" region that announces on step changes: "Step X of 3: {stepName}".
decisions.rationale: This defines explicit semantics and announcements without adding step-click navigation that is not specified. It conservatively improves screen reader understanding of progress and current position using standard patterns (nav, list, aria-current, aria-live).
decisions.sourceGap: Step indicator semantics and announcements are undefined (e.g., current step conveyed to screen readers, progress text, aria-current)

decisions.decision: Use standard Tab navigation with no focus trapping. Back/Next are native <button type="button"> elements and activate via Enter/Space by default. On Next/Back step change, programmatically move focus to the new step's <h2> heading (tabIndex="-1"). On validation failure, prevent navigation and move focus to the first invalid field; also set aria-invalid="true" on invalid controls and associate each error message via aria-describedby.
decisions.rationale: This fully specifies keyboard model and focus behavior with conventional, testable rules, avoiding custom keybindings or traps that could reduce accessibility. It also ensures errors are discoverable and focus is placed predictably.
decisions.sourceGap: Keyboard navigation model is unspecified (tab order across step content and Back/Next, Enter/Space activation, step changes not trapping focus)

decisions.decision: On first load, default to Step 1 (Personal info). The Back button is disabled (disabled attribute) on Step 1. Step indicator reflects Step 1 as current.
decisions.rationale: This resolves the initial wizard state and Back disabled behavior with the most conservative linear wizard pattern and no assumptions about prior progress.
decisions.sourceGap: Initial wizard state is unspecified (which step is default on first load, whether previously completed steps are prefilled)

decisions.decision: Treat each step as required to proceed. Next is disabled until the current step is valid. Validation runs on blur and on Next click; errors render inline beneath fields. Minimum validity rules: Personal info step requires non-empty "Legal first name", "Legal last name", and "Date of birth" (date input). Document upload step requires at least one successfully added file that passes client-side validation. Selfie step requires one selfie image provided via capture or upload.
decisions.rationale: This defines concrete gating and minimal schemas needed to implement and test the wizard flow without inventing extensive field sets. It uses conservative required-only inputs consistent with typical KYC steps.
decisions.sourceGap: Per-step validation states are missing (required fields, inline errors, and blocking Next until valid)

decisions.decision: Implement a single drop zone that is also keyboard-operable: the drop zone is a <button type="button"> styled as a panel with label text "Upload documents" and instructions "Drag and drop or choose files". Activating it opens a hidden <input type="file" multiple accept=".pdf,.jpg,.jpeg,.png,application/pdf,image/jpeg,image/png">. The button uses aria-describedby to reference instruction text and any error text. Drag-and-drop is additive; file picker is always available as the accessible alternative.
decisions.rationale: This explicitly provides a keyboard-accessible alternative and clear labeling for the drop target, meeting the drag-and-drop accessibility gaps while staying within the specified upload methods.
decisions.sourceGap: File upload drop zone accessibility is undefined (keyboard-operable alternative to drag-and-drop, clear label/instructions, ARIA for drop target)

decisions.decision: Allow up to 5 files. Enforce client-side constraints: allowed types PDF/JPG/PNG and max size 10MB per file. On invalid type or oversize, reject the file, show an inline error summary within the upload step (role="alert") and a per-file error row. Error messages are referenced from the file input via aria-describedby. Detect duplicates by matching name+size and reject with "This file was already added".
decisions.rationale: This resolves missing limits and error handling with conservative bounds and deterministic rules, enabling consistent UI, tests, and accessibility associations without requiring backend behavior assumptions.
decisions.sourceGap: Document upload error states are missing (file too large, unsupported type, upload failed, network error, duplicate file)

decisions.decision: On add, files enter an "uploading" state with an indeterminate progress indicator per file and a "Remove" action available at all times. While any file is uploading, Next is disabled and shows a loading label "Uploading…". If an upload fails, the file row shows "Upload failed" with a "Retry" action; Next remains disabled until all remaining files are in a successful state or removed.
decisions.rationale: This specifies in-progress, failure, retry, and navigation locking behavior required for a robust upload step without inventing server-specific progress APIs.
decisions.sourceGap: Document upload in-progress state is unspecified (uploading indicator, per-file progress, cancel/remove)

decisions.decision: Provide two options in the selfie step: "Use camera" and "Upload a photo". Camera path: show live preview (16:9 container that scales responsively), buttons "Capture" and "Retake" (native buttons). If permission is denied or camera unavailable, automatically switch to the upload option and display an inline message "Camera unavailable. Upload a selfie instead." Upload path accepts .jpg/.jpeg/.png up to 10MB and shows a preview with "Remove/Replace".
decisions.rationale: This defines a complete, accessible selfie collection approach including denied/unavailable states and a non-camera fallback, aligning with the gap without over-specifying UI beyond necessary controls.
decisions.sourceGap: Selfie step states are missing (camera permission denied, camera unavailable, capture in progress, retake, upload fallback)

decisions.decision: On Step 3 Next, perform a final submission request. During submission, disable Back/Next and change Next label to "Submitting…". On submission success, replace step content with the verification status view defaulting to "Pending review". On API failure (fetch existing status or submit), render a global inline error banner at the top of the wizard (role="alert") with text "Something went wrong. Please try again." and a "Retry" button that repeats the failed request.
decisions.rationale: This explicitly defines the missing submission state and global error handling with a simple retry mechanism, enabling deterministic UX and test coverage without assuming complex backend flows.
decisions.sourceGap: Final submission state is missing (submitting KYC package before status is shown)

decisions.decision: Render status with both icon and text: Pending review (clock icon), Approved (check icon), Rejected (x icon). Include a screen-reader label that announces "Verification status: {status}". For Rejected, display a "Reason" text block if provided by API; if no reason is available, show "Reason: Not provided". For Rejected, also show a primary action "Start over" that resets the wizard to Step 1 and clears step data in local state.
decisions.rationale: This resolves reliance on color alone and defines a conservative rejection follow-up that does not assume partial editability; it provides a clear next action and works whether or not a reason is returned.
decisions.sourceGap: Rejected status follow-up state is unspecified (whether rejection includes reason text and what user can do next)

decisions.decision: For widths < 480px: step indicator stacks vertically with full-width items and wraps long labels to multiple lines (no truncation). Back/Next actions become a sticky bottom bar with Back on the left and Next on the right, each min-height 44px. Document upload drop zone becomes full-width with min-height 120px and tap targets (buttons) at least 44px tall. Uploaded files render as a vertical list with filename wrapping and actions in a trailing overflow menu if needed. Verification status content stacks: icon+status on first row, message/reason below, actions full-width.
decisions.rationale: This defines concrete mobile behavior for wrapping, sizing, and action placement using conservative accessibility-friendly sizing and avoiding truncation that could hide critical info.
decisions.sourceGap: Layout rules for small screens are unspecified (step indicator wrapping/stacking, placement of Back/Next actions, and spacing between sections)

flows.completionCriteria: User completes all 3 steps, final submission succeeds, and verification status view is shown with status "Pending review".
flows.name: Complete KYC in the most direct path (pending review)

steps.action: Open the KYC verification wizard.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard loads on Step 1 (Personal info); step indicator shows Step 1 as current with aria-current="step"; Back is disabled; an aria-live polite region is ready to announce step changes.

steps.action: Enter required personal info fields.
steps.expectedResult: Fields validate on blur; no inline errors remain; Next becomes enabled because the step is valid.
steps.inputData: Legal first name, Legal last name, Date of birth

steps.action: Activate Next to go to Document upload.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard navigates to Step 2; focus moves to the Step 2 <h2> heading; aria-live announces "Step 2 of 3: Document upload"; step indicator updates current step.

steps.action: Add a valid document using the file picker.
steps.expectedResult: Selected file (PDF/JPG/PNG, <=10MB) is added (up to 5 allowed) and begins uploading; a per-file uploading indicator appears; Next becomes disabled and shows "Uploading…" while upload is in progress; file row offers Remove.

steps.action: Wait for document upload to complete successfully.
steps.expectedResult: File row updates to successful state; step is valid (at least one successful file); Next becomes enabled and returns to normal label.

steps.action: Activate Next to go to Selfie.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard navigates to Step 3; focus moves to the Step 3 <h2> heading; aria-live announces "Step 3 of 3: Selfie"; step indicator updates current step.

steps.action: Upload a selfie image.
steps.expectedResult: Selfie preview is shown with Remove/Replace; step becomes valid; Next becomes enabled.

steps.action: Activate Next to submit the KYC package.
steps.expectedResult: Final submission begins; Back/Next are disabled; Next label changes to "Submitting…".

steps.action: Wait for submission success and status display.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard replaces step content with verification status view defaulting to "Pending review" with icon+text (not color-only) and a screen-reader label "Verification status: Pending review".

flows.completionCriteria: User explores navigation (Back/Next), uses drag-and-drop and remove/replace, resolves an upload failure via retry, and completes submission to reach the verification status view.
flows.name: Explore steps, adjust uploads, handle retry, then submit successfully

steps.action: Open the KYC verification wizard on a small screen width (<480px).
steps.expectedResult: Step indicator stacks vertically with wrapped labels; Back/Next appear in a sticky bottom bar with >=44px height; wizard starts on Step 1 with Back disabled.

steps.action: Attempt to activate Next without completing required personal info.
steps.expectedResult: Navigation is prevented; inline errors render under required fields; focus moves to the first invalid field with aria-invalid="true" and error text associated via aria-describedby.

steps.action: Fill in personal info, then activate Next.
steps.expectedResult: Errors clear; Next is enabled; on step change focus moves to Step 2 heading; aria-live announces "Step 2 of 3: Document upload".
steps.inputData: Legal first name, Legal last name, Date of birth

steps.action: Add two documents using drag-and-drop onto the upload drop zone.
steps.expectedResult: Files are added additively; each appears with an uploading indicator and a Remove action; Next is disabled and shows "Uploading…" while any file is uploading.
steps.inputData: Two valid files (e.g., 1 PDF + 1 JPG, each <=10MB)

steps.action: Remove one of the uploading/added files.
steps.expectedResult: Removed file disappears from the list; validation recalculates based on remaining files; Next remains disabled until remaining uploads complete successfully.

steps.action: Observe one remaining file fail uploading, then press Retry for that file.
steps.expectedResult: File row shows "Upload failed" and a Retry action; on Retry, file returns to uploading state; Next stays disabled until upload succeeds or file is removed.

steps.action: Wait for the remaining upload to succeed, then activate Next.
steps.expectedResult: Once at least one file is successful, Next enables; wizard navigates to Step 3 with focus on Step 3 heading; aria-live announces "Step 3 of 3: Selfie".

steps.action: Select "Use camera" and attempt to start camera capture.
steps.expectedResult: If camera permission is denied or unavailable, UI automatically switches to upload option and shows inline message "Camera unavailable. Upload a selfie instead."; step remains invalid until a selfie is provided.

steps.action: Upload a selfie image, then activate Back to review documents.
steps.expectedResult: Selfie preview appears and step becomes valid; on Back, wizard navigates to Step 2; focus moves to Step 2 heading; aria-live announces "Step 2 of 3: Document upload"; previously added successful document remains listed.

steps.action: Activate Next to return to Selfie and confirm the selfie is still present.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard returns to Step 3; focus moves to Step 3 heading; selfie preview remains present; Next is enabled.

steps.action: Activate Next to submit; on transient API failure, press Retry; then complete submission.
steps.expectedResult: On submit, Back/Next are disabled and Next shows "Submitting…"; if API fails, a global error banner (role="alert") appears with "Something went wrong. Please try again." and a Retry button; pressing Retry repeats submission; on success, status view is shown (default Pending review) with icon+text and SR label.

flows.completionCriteria: User triggers client-side document validation errors (unsupported type and oversize), cannot proceed until a valid upload succeeds, then reaches Step 3.
flows.name: Document upload rejects invalid files and blocks Next until fixed

steps.action: Complete Step 1 with valid personal info and navigate to Step 2.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard is on Document upload step; focus is on Step 2 heading; drop zone button is available with instructions text referenced via aria-describedby.

steps.action: Activate the upload drop zone button to open the file picker.
steps.expectedResult: Native file picker opens via the hidden input; drop zone remains keyboard operable.

steps.action: Select an unsupported file type (e.g., .docx).
steps.expectedResult: File is rejected client-side; an inline error summary appears (role="alert") and a per-file error row indicates unsupported type; error text is associated to the input via aria-describedby; Next remains disabled because step is invalid.

steps.action: Select an oversize supported-type file (>10MB PDF/JPG/PNG).
steps.expectedResult: File is rejected with an oversize error; error summary updates; Next remains disabled.

steps.action: Select a valid supported file under 10MB.
steps.expectedResult: Valid file is added and begins uploading; per-file uploading indicator appears; Next remains disabled and shows "Uploading…" while upload is in progress.

steps.action: Wait for the valid file upload to complete successfully.
steps.expectedResult: File row shows successful state; step becomes valid (at least one successful file); Next becomes enabled; prior error summary may remain until dismissed/cleared by state update but no longer blocks progression.

steps.action: Activate Next to proceed to Step 3.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard navigates to Selfie step; focus moves to Step 3 heading; aria-live announces "Step 3 of 3: Selfie"; step indicator updates current step.

flows.completionCriteria: User attempts to add the same file twice, sees duplicate rejection, removes the existing file, re-adds successfully, and can proceed.
flows.name: Duplicate document detection and recovery

steps.action: Navigate to Document upload step with Step 1 already valid.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard shows Step 2; Next is disabled until at least one successful file exists.

steps.action: Add a valid document file via file picker.
steps.expectedResult: File appears and uploads; Next shows "Uploading…" until upload completes.

steps.action: Wait for upload to complete.
steps.expectedResult: File row is successful; Next becomes enabled.

steps.action: Attempt to add the same file again (same name and size).
steps.expectedResult: Duplicate is rejected; inline error summary (role="alert") shows "This file was already added" and/or a per-file error row; existing successful file remains unchanged; Next remains enabled because at least one successful file still exists.

steps.action: Remove the existing successful file, then add the file again.
steps.expectedResult: After removal, step becomes invalid and Next disables; re-adding starts upload and Next shows "Uploading…"; after success, Next re-enables.

steps.action: Activate Next to proceed to Selfie step.
steps.expectedResult: Wizard navigates to Step 3; focus moves to Step 3 heading; aria-live announces step change.

contractCompatibilityIssues: kyc_verification_wizard: passes a no-op handler for `on_camera_unavailable`, which breaks callback wiring.
kyc_verification_wizard: passes a no-op handler for `on_capture_selfie`, which breaks callback wiring.
kyc_verification_wizard: passes a no-op handler for `on_retake_selfie`, which breaks callback wiring.
personal_info_step: callback `on_blur` from the interface is never invoked in generated files.
verification_status: callback `on_start_over` from the interface is never invoked in generated files.

kyc_verification_wizard: emits callbacks as on_step_change/on_submit_start/on_submit_success/on_submit_error/on_start_over props, but the interface specifies returns/emits named step_change/submit_start/submit_success/submit_error/start_over; event contract naming does not match the provided componentInterfaces.

kyc_verification_wizard: does not pass required props (max_files, max_file_size_bytes, accepted_file_types) to document_upload_step as required by its interface; current usage only passes files/is_uploading/is_disabled/on_add_files/on_remove_file/on_retry_file.

kyc_verification_wizard: document_upload_step expects KycDocumentUploadItem with optional error_message, but wizard maps files without error_message, so per-file error messaging cannot display via the child component contract.

kyc_verification_wizard: passes camera_unavailable_message={null} and provides an on_camera_unavailable callback that is a no-op; e2e expects a visible fallback message "Camera unavailable. Upload a selfie instead." when camera unavailable, which cannot occur with current wiring.

kyc_verification_wizard: verification_status component interface returns/emits start_over, but implementation only uses on_start_over prop callback; event naming mismatch with interface returns/emits.

accepts.description: Transaction status value used to determine label and styling. Supported: "pending", "completed", "failed", "refunded". Any other value renders the neutral "Unknown" badge.

accepts.name: transactions

accepts.description: Total number of transactions available on the server for the current query context; used to compute total pages.
accepts.name: total_count

accepts.description: Whether the initial load is in progress; when true the table renders a skeleton with header visible and placeholder rows.
accepts.name: is_initial_loading

accepts.description: Whether a reload fetch is in progress due to sort/pagination changes; when true, keep current rows visible, show loading overlay, and disable sort and pagination controls.
accepts.name: is_fetching

accepts.description: Whether the table is in an error state for the last fetch attempt; when true, show the error row spanning all columns and a Retry button.
accepts.name: has_error

accepts.description: Current error message to display when has_error is true. If omitted, component uses default copy: "Unable to load transactions."
accepts.name: error_message

accepts.description: Current 1-based page index.
accepts.name: current_page

accepts.description: Current page size; allowed values are 25, 50, or 100.
accepts.name: page_size

accepts.name: sort_key

accepts.description: Current sort direction for sort_key.

accepts.description: Callback invoked when the user changes pages via pagination controls (First/Previous/Next/Last).
accepts.name: on_page_change

accepts.description: Callback invoked when the user changes page size; caller should reset to page 1 and refetch while preserving current sort.
accepts.name: on_page_size_change

accepts.name: on_retry

returns.description: Emitted when user requests a page change via pagination controls.

returns.description: Emitted when user requests a page size change (25/50/100); intended to reset to page 1.

accessibilityGaps: Sorting controls are not specified as keyboard-operable header buttons with proper aria-sort and accessible names
Row-click interaction lacks keyboard equivalent (Enter/Space) and focusable row/interactive element semantics
Focus visible styling is not specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls
Status badge relies on color but no non-color cue requirements (text already present, but contrast/forced-colors behavior not defined)
Pagination controls lack defined ARIA labels (e.g., next/previous, page size selector, current page announcement)
missingStates: Table loading state (initial load and reloading on sort/paginate)
Table empty state when there are no transactions
Table error state when data fetch fails (and retry behavior)
Sorting state details: default sort column/direction, unsorted state, and sort direction indicator behavior
Row hover/active/selected state styling (especially for clickable rows)
Disabled/unavailable pagination states (first/prev disabled on first page; next/last disabled on last page)
Page size change behavior state: whether changing page size resets to page 1 and how selection is reflected
Unknown/unsupported status fallback state (if API returns a status outside pending/completed/failed/refunded)
recommendations: Define sort UX spec: default sort, whether multi-sort is allowed, toggle order (none→asc→desc or asc↔desc), and header iconography
Implement sortable headers as buttons with aria-sort and screen-reader text indicating current sort column and direction
Make row navigation accessible by providing a dedicated 'View details' link/button in a cell or make the row a focusable element with Enter/Space activation and clear focus ring
Specify loading UX (skeleton vs spinner), including whether table keeps previous rows during resort/repaginate (stale-while-revalidate) and how interactions are disabled during loading
Add explicit empty and error render paths with actionable messaging and a retry control
Define pagination model precisely: total count availability, total pages calculation, current page display format, and behavior when total changes
Specify status badge design tokens beyond color (text color, background, border, contrast targets, forced-colors/high-contrast handling) and a fallback styling for unknown statuses
Document interactive state styles (hover/pressed/selected) for rows, header buttons, and pagination elements to ensure consistent implementation
responsiveGaps: No rules for handling narrow viewports: whether columns wrap, truncate with ellipsis, or collapse into a stacked/card layout
No priority order for hiding/reordering columns on small screens (e.g., payment method vs merchant name)
No specification for horizontal scrolling vs responsive reflow when all 5 columns do not fit
No guidance on long content overflow (merchant names, payment method strings) and max widths per column
Pagination placement and layout on mobile (stacking page size selector and navigation, touch target sizing) are not defined

coveredBehaviors: Composed sort->fetching reload state: sortable headers emit sort-change payloads; parent updates sort props; table reflects aria-sort and disables header/pagination while fetching

Composed pagination->fetching reload state: pagination controls emit page-change and page-size-change payloads; parent updates paging props; pagination boundary states and aria-live page text update after refetch
Row-level details opening via pointer row-click and keyboard-accessible per-row "View details" control; callback payload wiring to parent handler
Error recovery integration: error state shows retry; retry triggers handler; parent re-attempts and then renders rows and pagination again
Unhappy invalid action prevention: attempting to paginate during in-flight fetch is blocked by disabled controls and does not emit additional callbacks
Status badge label is present in composed rows, including unknown-status fallback label
coveredStates: Pagination state (page X of Y, boundary disabled/enabled)

parsing.businessContext: Display and browse transactions in a tabular view with sortable columns, paginated results, status badges, and row-level access to transaction details.

Allowed status values: pending, completed, failed, refunded.

User paginates through the transaction list and can change page size to 25/50/100.
Clicking a row opens transaction details.

decisions.decision: Implement each sortable column header as a <button type="button"> inside the <th>. The button accessible name is "Sort by {ColumnName}". Maintain sort state in the table as {sortKey, sortDirection}. Apply aria-sort to the <th> of the active sort column only: "ascending" or "descending"; all other headers have no aria-sort attribute. The header button shows a visual sort indicator (up/down chevron) and includes visually-hidden text that announces "sorted ascending/descending" for the active column.
decisions.rationale: This makes sorting explicitly keyboard-operable and screen-reader discoverable using standard table semantics with aria-sort, while keeping the rest of the headers neutral. Using a button in the header is the most conservative, widely supported pattern for interactive sorting.
decisions.sourceGap: Sorting controls are not specified as keyboard-operable header buttons with proper aria-sort and accessible names

decisions.decision: Default sort is Date descending on initial render. Sorting is single-column only (no multi-sort). Clicking/activating a header toggles direction between ascending and descending for that column; selecting a different column sets that column to ascending on first activation. There is no unsorted state once data is shown.
decisions.rationale: Defines deterministic sorting behavior needed for implementation and testing. Choosing a common default (most recent first) and a simple two-state toggle avoids ambiguous "none" state handling and multi-sort complexity.
decisions.sourceGap: Sorting state details: default sort column/direction, unsorted state, and sort direction indicator behavior

decisions.decision: Do not make the entire <tr> focusable. Add a dedicated "View details" action as the last focusable element within each row (e.g., a <a> or <button>) with accessible name "View details for transaction {merchant} on {date}" (fallback to "View transaction details" if values missing). Mouse click anywhere on the row also triggers the same action, but keyboard access is provided via the dedicated control.
decisions.rationale: Provides a clear, standard keyboard path without relying on nonstandard focusable row semantics, while preserving the brief’s row-click convenience for pointer users. This conservatively reduces accessibility risk and complexity.
decisions.sourceGap: Row-click interaction lacks keyboard equivalent (Enter/Space) and focusable row/interactive element semantics

decisions.decision: Apply a visible focus indicator to sortable header buttons, the per-row "View details" control, and all pagination controls using :focus-visible. The focus ring must be at least 2px and not removed; it must be visible against both header and body backgrounds.
decisions.rationale: Explicitly defines focus-visible styling targets so downstream implementation and QA can verify keyboard navigation. Keeping the requirement generic (thickness/visibility) is conservative given missing design tokens.
decisions.sourceGap: Focus visible styling is not specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls

decisions.decision: Status badge must always render the status text label (Pending/Completed/Failed/Refunded) and never rely on color alone. In forced-colors/high-contrast mode, render the badge with a 1px solid border using currentColor and transparent background; ensure text remains visible (use CanvasText/currentColor). Maintain a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for text against badge background in normal mode.
decisions.rationale: Resolves the non-color cue and high-contrast ambiguity with a standard, testable approach that works across themes and forced-colors modes while preserving the existing text cue.
decisions.sourceGap: Status badge relies on color but no non-color cue requirements (text already present, but contrast/forced-colors behavior not defined)

decisions.decision: If the API returns a status outside pending/completed/failed/refunded, render a neutral badge labeled "Unknown" using the same badge shape and typography, with a gray/neutral styling distinct from the known statuses.
decisions.rationale: Prevents rendering failures and ensures consistent UI when backend expands statuses. Using a neutral "Unknown" is conservative and avoids misrepresenting the status.
decisions.sourceGap: Unknown/unsupported status fallback state (if API returns a status outside pending/completed/failed/refunded)

decisions.decision: Provide a loading state: on initial load, render a table skeleton with header visible and 10 placeholder rows. On sort or pagination changes, keep existing rows visible and show an inline loading overlay (or row-level skeleton) while fetching; disable header sort buttons and pagination controls during the fetch to prevent concurrent requests.
decisions.rationale: Defines both initial and reloading behaviors and avoids flicker by keeping prior content while updating. Disabling interactions during fetch is conservative and simplifies state management and testing.
decisions.sourceGap: Table loading state (initial load and reloading on sort/paginate)

decisions.decision: If there are zero transactions after loading completes, render an empty state in the table body area that spans all columns with message: "No transactions to display." Keep the table header visible and keep pagination hidden/disabled when total count is 0.
decisions.rationale: Provides a clear, minimal empty state without inventing filtering or onboarding content. Keeping headers visible maintains context and reduces layout shift.
decisions.sourceGap: Table empty state when there are no transactions

decisions.decision: If data fetch fails, render an error state in the table body area spanning all columns with message: "Unable to load transactions." Provide a "Retry" button that re-attempts the last request (same sort/page/pageSize).
decisions.rationale: Defines an actionable error path and a deterministic retry behavior needed for implementation and automated tests, without adding extra recovery flows.
decisions.sourceGap: Table error state when data fetch fails (and retry behavior)

decisions.decision: For pointer users, rows show hover styling (subtle background change) indicating clickability. When the row’s "View details" control is active/pressed, show a pressed state on that control (not on the entire row). No persistent "selected" row state is used in the table.
decisions.rationale: Resolves ambiguity around hover/active/selected states while avoiding introducing a selection model not mentioned in the brief.
decisions.sourceGap: Row hover/active/selected state styling (especially for clickable rows)

decisions.decision: Pagination is server-driven and requires totalCount from the data source. Compute totalPages = ceil(totalCount / pageSize). Display current page as "Page X of Y". If totalCount changes and the current page exceeds totalPages, clamp current page to totalPages and refetch.
decisions.rationale: Defines a precise, testable pagination model and handles dynamic totals conservatively by clamping to the last valid page instead of erroring or showing empty pages unexpectedly.
decisions.sourceGap: Define pagination model precisely: total count availability, total pages calculation, current page display format, and behavior when total changes

decisions.decision: Provide First/Previous/Next/Last controls. Disable First and Previous when currentPage == 1. Disable Next and Last when currentPage == totalPages or totalPages == 0. Disabled controls are not focusable and use aria-disabled only if rendered as non-button elements; prefer native disabled buttons.
decisions.rationale: Explicitly defines boundary behavior and a conservative accessibility-friendly implementation using native disabled semantics.
decisions.sourceGap: Disabled/unavailable pagination states (first/prev disabled on first page; next/last disabled on last page)

decisions.decision: Page size selector offers 25, 50, 100. Changing page size resets currentPage to 1 and triggers a refetch with the current sort settings preserved. The selector reflects the active page size value.
decisions.rationale: Resetting to page 1 is the most predictable behavior and avoids landing on an out-of-range page after a page size change.
decisions.sourceGap: Page size change behavior state: whether changing page size resets to page 1 and how selection is reflected

decisions.decision: Add aria-labels: First="First page", Previous="Previous page", Next="Next page", Last="Last page". Page size select has label "Rows per page". Add an aria-live="polite" region that announces "Page {X} of {Y}" after pagination changes and "Sorted by {ColumnName} {Direction}" after sort changes.
decisions.rationale: Resolves missing ARIA labeling and provides minimal announcements for state changes without overcomplicating the UI with verbose narration.
decisions.sourceGap: Pagination controls lack defined ARIA labels (e.g., next/previous, page size selector, current page announcement)

decisions.decision: On narrow viewports, keep the table layout (no card/stacked conversion) and enable horizontal scrolling by wrapping the table in an overflow-x:auto container. For Merchant Name and Payment Method cells, truncate with ellipsis (white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis) and show full content via native title attribute. Date, Amount, and Status do not wrap. No columns are hidden or reordered responsively.
decisions.rationale: Chooses the least disruptive responsive strategy consistent with a table component and avoids speculative column priority/hiding rules. Ellipsis + title is a conservative overflow solution requiring no additional components.
decisions.sourceGap: No rules for handling narrow viewports: whether columns wrap, truncate with ellipsis, or collapse into a stacked/card layout

coveredBehaviors: Renders a non-color status text label for each supported status (pending/completed/failed/refunded).
Falls back to a neutral "Unknown" badge label when provided an unsupported status value.
Applies status-specific styling hooks (data-status and/or className) for supported statuses and unknown fallback.
Renders table headers for Date/Amount/Status/Merchant Name/Payment Method with sortable header buttons named "Sort by {Column}"
Invokes on_sort_change with asc when a different column is chosen; toggles asc/desc when the same column is activated again
Applies aria-sort="ascending"/"descending" only to the active sorted column header cell
Initial loading: renders a skeleton/placeholder state while keeping the header visible
Fetching reload: keeps current rows visible while disabling sort buttons and pagination controls
Row click triggers on_open_details with the transaction payload/id
Per-row "View details" control triggers on_open_details and has an accessible name that includes merchant and date when available
Error state renders default copy when error_message is not provided and exposes a Retry button that calls on_retry
Empty state renders "No transactions to display." spanning all columns and hides/disables pagination when total_count is 0
Pagination wiring: forwards on_page_change from pagination controls and on_page_size_change from rows-per-page selector
Computes total pages as ceil(total_count / page_size) and displays "Page X of Y"
Disables First/Previous on first page and Next/Last on last page (native disabled buttons)
Invokes on_page_change with requested page when First/Previous/Next/Last are activated
Disables all pagination controls and rows-per-page selector when is_loading is true and prevents callbacks
Renders rows-per-page selector labeled "Rows per page" with default options [25,50,100] when page_size_options not provided
Uses provided page_size_options when passed
Invokes on_page_size_change when user selects a new page size
Supports total_count=0 state (total pages 0) and disables navigation

steps.action: Wait for the transaction table to finish initial loading.
steps.expectedResult: Skeleton placeholders are replaced by real transaction rows; default sort is Date descending.

flows.completionCriteria: User successfully changes sort, changes page size, navigates pages, and opens transaction details for a specific row.
flows.name: Explore transactions with sorting and pagination before opening details

steps.action: Wait for the transaction table to finish initial loading.
steps.expectedResult: Table renders with rows and status badges; default sort is Date descending; pagination shows "Page 1 of Y" when totalCount > 0.

steps.action: Activate the Amount column header sort button.
steps.expectedResult: Sort changes to Amount ascending; active header <th> has aria-sort="ascending"; other headers have no aria-sort; an aria-live message announces "Sorted by Amount ascending"; sort/pagination controls are disabled while the fetch runs and then re-enabled when results update.

steps.action: Activate the Amount column header sort button again.
steps.expectedResult: Sort toggles to Amount descending; aria-sort updates to "descending"; aria-live announces "Sorted by Amount descending"; table updates after loading overlay completes.

steps.action: Change the page size to 50 using the rows-per-page selector.
steps.expectedResult: Page size updates to 50; currentPage resets to 1; fetch runs with current sort preserved; aria-live announces "Page 1 of Y" after update; pagination boundary disabled states update accordingly.

steps.action: Click Next page.
steps.expectedResult: Current page increments by 1; table updates after loading overlay; aria-live announces updated "Page X of Y"; First/Previous become enabled if leaving page 1.

steps.action: Inspect a row's Status badge text label.
steps.expectedResult: Badge shows a text label (Pending/Completed/Failed/Refunded), ensuring status is not color-only; if status is unrecognized, a neutral "Unknown" badge is shown.

steps.action: Use keyboard Tab to focus the row's "View details" control and press Enter.
steps.expectedResult: "View details" control shows a visible :focus-visible ring; activating it opens the transaction details view; control accessible name includes merchant and date when available.

flows.completionCriteria: Second pagination action is prevented while loading, and after load completes the user can paginate successfully.
flows.name: User attempts pagination actions while a fetch is in progress

steps.action: Wait for the transaction table to finish initial loading.
steps.expectedResult: Table renders rows and pagination; controls are enabled.

steps.action: Click Next page to trigger a pagination fetch.
steps.expectedResult: Pagination fetch begins; pagination controls and sortable header buttons become disabled until the fetch completes; loading overlay is shown while prior rows remain visible.

steps.action: Immediately click Next page again while controls are disabled.
steps.expectedResult: No second request is initiated; currentPage does not change again; UI remains in the same loading state until the in-flight fetch completes.

steps.action: After loading completes, click Next page again.
steps.expectedResult: A new fetch runs; page advances by 1; aria-live announces updated "Page X of Y"; controls reflect correct disabled/enabled boundary states after update.

flows.completionCriteria: After a failed fetch, user retries and the table successfully renders transaction rows.
flows.name: Handle data fetch error and recover via retry

steps.action: Open the transactions view and allow the initial data request to fail.
steps.expectedResult: Table header remains visible; table body shows error state spanning all columns with message "Unable to load transactions." and a "Retry" button.

steps.action: Click the "Retry" button.
steps.expectedResult: The last request is re-attempted using the same sort/page/pageSize; loading UI appears; sort and pagination controls are disabled during the fetch.

steps.action: Wait for the retry request to succeed.
steps.expectedResult: Error state is replaced by transaction rows; pagination renders if totalCount > 0; default/saved sort state is applied and reflected via aria-sort on the active column.

contractCompatibilityIssues: transaction_table: callback `on_retry` from the interface is never invoked in generated files.

transaction_pagination: exports default function only, but transaction_table imports a named export { TransactionPagination } from '../TransactionPagination/TransactionPagination', causing an integration/runtime failure.

transaction_pagination: on_page_change payload shape does not match interface; componentInterfaces expects (payload: PageChangePayload) => void where payload is PageChangePayload, but implementation emits { current_page } only (no support for { page } alias used by unit tests/mocks).

transaction_pagination: on_page_size_change payload shape does not match interface; componentInterfaces expects PageSizeChangePayload with page_size plus page/current_page (reset to 1), but implementation emits { page_size } only.
transaction_pagination: page_size prop type is number in implementation, but interface constrains it to 25 | 50 | 100.
issuesFound: transaction_table: callback `on_retry` from the interface is never invoked in generated files.

Deterministic token compliance is true and no hallucinated tokens were detected; however, transaction_table uses non-tokenized color 'rgba(243, 244, 246, 0.55)' for the fetching overlay background (token compliance should be re-checked in codegen rules if strict token-only colors are required).

transaction_table: row click opens details for pointer users, but the row itself is not keyboard-focusable; keyboard path exists only via per-row 'View details' button (acceptable per resolving decision, but row-click behavior is not equivalently available to keyboard users).
transaction_table: fetch overlay is aria-hidden and provides no aria-busy or live announcement of loading state; screen reader users may miss reload feedback.
transaction_pagination: contract mismatch and incorrect exports block integration and will likely fail tests and composed usage.

accepts.description: Current 1-based page index to display (used for 'Page X of Y' and to disable/enable Previous/Next).

accepts.description: Current page size selection. Must be one of the allowed page sizes (25/50/100).

accessibilityGaps: Define keyboard interaction for sortable headers (tab focus, Enter/Space to sort) and announce sort state via aria-sort
Row click opens details but no accessible affordance is defined (e.g., row as link/button with role and accessible name) or alternative action for keyboard users
Pagination controls need explicit labeling for screen readers (current page, next/previous, page size selector) and focus order behavior
Status conveyed by color only is possible; specify text/aria-label remains present and ensure badge meaning is announced non-visually
Specify focus-visible styling for interactive elements (headers, rows, pagination) to meet keyboard usability
missingStates: Loading state for initial fetch and for sort/pagination transitions (skeleton/placeholder vs spinner)
Empty state when there are no transactions (and whether headers/pagination remain visible)
Error state for failed data fetch (and retry behavior)
No-results state when the dataset is empty due to filtering/search (even if filtering is out of scope, clarify if applicable or omit)
Disabled states for pagination at boundaries (first/last page) and for unavailable page size options
Unknown/unsupported status value handling (fallback badge style/label)
recommendations: Specify table column data formats and alignment rules: date format/timezone, currency formatting for amount, right/left alignment, and negative/zero handling
Define sorting rules per column: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggling, stable sort behavior, and how null/blank values sort
Define pagination UI specifics: which controls appear (prev/next, first/last, page numbers), where the 25/50/100 selector lives, and whether page resets to 1 when page size changes
Clarify the navigation pattern for row click: opens modal drawer vs new page/route, whether middle-click/new-tab is supported, and whether there is a dedicated 'View details' action
Provide explicit status-to-style mapping (badge background/text colors) and contrast requirements; include fallback styling for unknown statuses
Document data overflow behavior per column (truncate with ellipsis, wrap, tooltip on hover/focus) especially for merchant name and payment method
responsiveGaps: Define small-screen behavior for 5-column table (horizontal scroll vs column stacking vs hiding lower-priority columns)
Specify how pagination layout adapts on mobile (page size selector placement, collapsing page numbers, sticky footer/header behavior)
Define responsive truncation/line-wrapping rules for long merchant names and payment methods to avoid layout breakage
Clarify minimum column widths and whether the table becomes scrollable within a container to prevent viewport overflow

coveredBehaviors: Composed loading -> loaded transition shows header throughout and disables/re-enables sorting and pagination appropriately
Keyboard sorting (Enter/Space) on header updates aria-sort and triggers parent sort change; parent re-renders with new sort and data
Pagination Next/Previous and page-size change propagate via callbacks; parent updates page/page_size (reset to page 1 on size change) while preserving sort; pagination aria-live text updates
Row overlay link accessible name and href generation (default and template override) and navigation-style behavior; emits details activation callback payload
Unhappy boundary action: disabled Previous on first page blocks action and does not trigger callbacks; recovery via Next works
Unhappy error state: renders error message and Retry; disables sorting/pagination; Retry triggers refetch and recovers to loaded

parsing.businessContext: View and browse a list of transactions with sorting, pagination, status indicators, and access to transaction details.

components.name: Transaction Table
components.purpose: Display transactions in a sortable, paginated table with status badges and row-level access to details.

components.name: Transaction Table Pagination
components.purpose: Control page navigation and page size for the transaction list.

components.name: Transaction Status Badge
components.purpose: Render a colored status badge for each transaction status value.

content.description: Transaction status column rendered with a colored badge.
content.name: Status

interactions.description: Sort transactions by the selected column.
Navigate between pages and change items per page (25/50/100).
Clicking a row opens the transaction details view.

tokenReferences.description: Badge colors mapped per status (pending, completed, failed, refunded).
tokenReferences.name: status color

decisions.decision: Implement each sortable column header as a focusable button within the <th>. Support Enter/Space to toggle sorting on that column. Apply aria-sort on the corresponding <th> with values "none" (unsorted), "ascending", or "descending"; only the actively sorted column has ascending/descending and all others are "none".
decisions.rationale: This defines a complete keyboard interaction and a standards-based announcement of sort state without changing the visual design requirements, enabling accessible sorting for all columns.
decisions.sourceGap: Define keyboard interaction for sortable headers (tab focus, Enter/Space to sort) and announce sort state via aria-sort

decisions.decision: Make the first cell in each row (Date) contain a full-row overlay anchor link styled to cover the row hit area. The link navigates to a details route pattern "/transactions/{transactionId}". The link accessible name is "View transaction {transactionId}". Preserve standard link behaviors (keyboard Enter, open in new tab via context menu/middle click).
decisions.rationale: Using a real link provides a clear, keyboard-accessible affordance for opening details and supports common navigation expectations conservatively without inventing a modal/drawer pattern.
decisions.sourceGap: Row click opens details but no accessible affordance is defined (e.g., row as link/button with role and accessible name) or alternative action for keyboard users

decisions.decision: Pagination includes: Previous button, Next button, and a page size <select> with options 25/50/100. Wrap controls in a <nav aria-label="Transaction table pagination">. Previous/Next have aria-label "Previous page" / "Next page" and use disabled=true at boundaries. Render current page text "Page X of Y" as an aria-live="polite" region that updates on page changes. Tab order is Previous -> Next -> Page size selector.
decisions.rationale: This specifies explicit labels, boundary disabled behavior, and a deterministic focus order while keeping the UI minimal and consistent with the brief (no requirement for page numbers/first/last).
decisions.sourceGap: Pagination controls need explicit labeling for screen readers (current page, next/previous, page size selector) and focus order behavior

decisions.decision: Always render the status text inside the badge (e.g., "Pending"). The badge element includes aria-label identical to the visible text. Do not rely on color to convey meaning; color is supplementary only.
decisions.rationale: Keeping status text present ensures non-visual users receive the same information and resolves the risk of color-only encoding without requiring extra UI elements.
decisions.sourceGap: Status conveyed by color only is possible; specify text/aria-label remains present and ensure badge meaning is announced non-visually

decisions.decision: Apply a consistent focus-visible ring to interactive elements: sortable header buttons, row overlay links, pagination buttons, and the page size select. Use a 2px outline with 2px offset and ensure it is visible on all status badge background colors.
decisions.rationale: Explicit focus-visible styling ensures keyboard usability across all interactive controls without prescribing a full theme, and it is a conservative accessibility baseline.
decisions.sourceGap: Specify focus-visible styling for interactive elements (headers, rows, pagination) to meet keyboard usability

decisions.decision: Add three table-level states: (1) Loading: show 10-row skeleton placeholders while retaining the table header; disable sorting and pagination controls. (2) Empty: show a single full-width row message "No transactions"; keep headers visible and hide pagination. (3) Error: show a full-width message "Transactions couldn’t be loaded" with a "Retry" button that re-triggers fetch; keep headers visible and disable sorting/pagination until success.
decisions.rationale: These states cover the primary data lifecycle gaps (loading/empty/error) in a way that preserves layout stability and defines control availability for downstream implementation and tests.
decisions.sourceGap: Loading state for initial fetch and for sort/pagination transitions (skeleton/placeholder vs spinner)

decisions.decision: Default sort is Date descending. Sorting is bi-state per column: selecting a column toggles ascending/descending; selecting a different column activates that column in ascending order. Sorting is stable. Null/blank values always sort last in both directions.
decisions.rationale: This fully specifies predictable sort rules (default, toggling, stability, null handling) with conservative choices commonly used in transaction tables.
decisions.sourceGap: Define sorting rules per column: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggling, stable sort behavior, and how null/blank values sort

decisions.decision: When page size changes (25/50/100), reset to page 1 and refetch/recompute the dataset for that new size. Keep the current sort applied.
decisions.rationale: Resetting to page 1 prevents out-of-range pages after size changes and preserves the user’s chosen ordering, minimizing surprises and edge cases.
decisions.sourceGap: Define pagination UI specifics: which controls appear (prev/next, first/last, page numbers), where the 25/50/100 selector lives, and whether page resets to 1 when page size changes

decisions.decision: Date displays as "YYYY-MM-DD" in the user’s local timezone. Amount displays as a currency formatted using the user locale with two decimal places; negative amounts display with a leading minus sign. Align Amount right; all other columns left.
decisions.rationale: This resolves formatting and alignment ambiguities with locale-safe defaults and conventional financial table alignment without requiring additional inputs.
decisions.sourceGap: Specify table column data formats and alignment rules: date format/timezone, currency formatting for amount, right/left alignment, and negative/zero handling

decisions.decision: Map statuses to badge styles: pending=amber, completed=green, failed=red, refunded=blue. Ensure text contrast meets WCAG AA for normal text. For unknown/unsupported status values, render a neutral gray badge with text "Unknown" and aria-label "Unknown".
decisions.rationale: This provides an explicit mapping plus an accessible fallback, preventing rendering failures when new status values appear.
decisions.sourceGap: Unknown/unsupported status value handling (fallback badge style/label)

decisions.decision: Merchant Name and Payment Method cells are single-line with truncation (ellipsis). On hover and keyboard focus, show a tooltip containing the full text; the cell also includes a title attribute with the full value as a baseline fallback.
decisions.rationale: This prevents layout breakage from long strings while still enabling access to the full content for mouse and keyboard users with a conservative fallback.
decisions.sourceGap: Document data overflow behavior per column (truncate with ellipsis, wrap, tooltip on hover/focus) especially for merchant name and payment method

decisions.decision: On small screens, keep the 5-column table and enable horizontal scrolling within a container (overflow-x:auto) rather than stacking/hiding columns. Set minimum widths: Date 120px, Amount 120px, Status 120px, Merchant Name 200px, Payment Method 160px. Pagination stays below the table; controls wrap to two lines if needed with page size selector on the second line.
decisions.rationale: Horizontal scroll is the most conservative responsive strategy for dense tabular data, and minimum widths prevent column collapse while keeping behavior deterministic for implementation.
decisions.sourceGap: Define small-screen behavior for 5-column table (horizontal scroll vs column stacking vs hiding lower-priority columns)

coveredBehaviors: Renders derived label text from supported `status` values (Pending/Completed/Failed/Refunded)
Renders neutral fallback label "Unknown" for unsupported status values
Uses `label` prop to override visible text regardless of status
Defaults `aria-label` to the visible label text when `aria_label` is not provided
Uses `aria_label` prop to override the accessible name while keeping visible label unchanged
Renders table column headers (Date, Amount, Status, Merchant Name, Payment Method)
Applies aria-sort="descending" to the active sorted column header (Date) and aria-sort="none" to others
Invokes on_sort_change on sortable header click with bi-state toggling when the active column is clicked again
Invokes on_sort_change on Enter/Space keydown on sortable header buttons
Disables sorting interactions while is_loading=true or is_error=true
Loading state renders 10 skeleton rows and keeps header visible
Error state renders error message and Retry button; Retry invokes on_retry; sorting/pagination disabled
Empty state renders "No transactions" and hides pagination
Renders row overlay link in Date cell with accessible name "View transaction {transactionId}"
Row overlay link href defaults to /transactions/{transactionId} and supports override via details_href_template
Emits details_link_activated event payload when overlay link is clicked
Amount cells are right-aligned
Merchant Name and Payment Method cells include title attributes with full text for overflow fallback
Renders pagination within a <nav> landmark labeled "Transaction table pagination"
Displays current page text "Page X of Y" and marks it aria-live="polite"
Previous/Next buttons have accessible names "Previous page" and "Next page"
Disables Previous button when current_page is 1
Disables Next button when current_page equals total_pages
Invokes on_previous_page when Previous is activated (when enabled)
Invokes on_next_page when Next is activated (when enabled)
Renders page size <select> with options 25/50/100 by default
Supports custom page_size_options prop for selector options
Invokes on_page_size_change with numeric payload when selection changes
When disabled=true, disables Previous/Next and page size selector and prevents callback invocations

steps.expectedResult: Transaction table initializes with default sort Date descending; loading state begins while data is fetched.

steps.action: Wait for the table data to load.
steps.expectedResult: Skeleton placeholders disappear; rows render with formatted Date (YYYY-MM-DD local timezone), Amount (localized currency, 2 decimals, right-aligned), Status badge text, Merchant Name and Payment Method truncated with ellipsis when long. Pagination controls render below if there are multiple pages.

steps.expectedResult: Browser navigates to the details route /transactions/{transactionId}; link behavior supports keyboard Enter and standard new-tab behavior.

steps.action: Navigate to the transactions list view where the transaction table is rendered.
steps.expectedResult: Transaction table initializes with default sort Date descending and begins loading with skeleton rows; sorting and pagination controls are disabled during loading.

steps.action: Wait for data to load.
steps.expectedResult: Rows render and interactive elements show focus-visible styling when tabbed to; the currently sorted column is Date with aria-sort="descending" and other headers aria-sort="none".

steps.action: Tab to the Amount column header sort button and press Enter.
steps.expectedResult: Active sort changes to Amount ascending (aria-sort="ascending" on Amount header, "none" on others). Table shows loading skeleton while applying sort; sorting and pagination are disabled during the transition. Null/blank amounts (if any) appear last. After load, rows are stably sorted.

steps.action: Press Space on the Amount column header sort button again.
steps.expectedResult: Sort toggles to Amount descending (aria-sort="descending"); table briefly shows loading skeleton and then updates with stable ordering and null/blank values last.

steps.action: Tab to the Next page button and activate it.
steps.expectedResult: Moves to the next page while keeping the current sort (Amount descending). The pagination region updates "Page X of Y" with aria-live="polite". Table shows loading skeleton during fetch; controls disabled until completion.

steps.action: Open the page size selector and choose 100.
steps.expectedResult: Page size changes to 100 and resets to page 1. Current sort (Amount descending) is preserved. "Page 1 of Y" updates in the aria-live region; table shows loading skeleton during refresh.

steps.action: Hover or focus a truncated Merchant Name cell to view the tooltip with full text.
steps.expectedResult: Tooltip displays the full Merchant Name for the focused/hovered cell; title attribute also provides a baseline full-text exposure.

steps.action: Activate the row overlay link for a chosen transaction on page 1.
steps.expectedResult: Navigates to /transactions/{transactionId} for the selected row via the accessible link.

flows.completionCriteria: User attempts an invalid pagination action at a boundary, receives no navigation due to disabled control, then successfully navigates using an enabled control and reaches a different page.
flows.name: Attempt to paginate past boundaries (disabled controls) then recover

steps.action: Navigate to the transactions list view where the transaction table is rendered and wait for it to load.
steps.expectedResult: Table shows rows (or a single page) with pagination visible when applicable; pagination nav has aria-label "Transaction table pagination" and shows "Page X of Y".

steps.action: Ensure the table is on the first page (Page 1 of Y).
steps.expectedResult: Previous button is rendered with disabled=true; Next button enabled when Y>1; "Page 1 of Y" is displayed.

steps.action: Attempt to activate the disabled Previous page button (click or keyboard Enter).
steps.expectedResult: No page change occurs; no fetch is triggered; focus remains stable on the control; current page text remains "Page 1 of Y".

steps.action: Activate the Next page button.
steps.expectedResult: Page increments to Page 2 of Y with aria-live="polite" announcement; table shows loading skeleton during fetch then renders new rows; Previous becomes enabled.

flows.completionCriteria: A failed fetch shows the error row and Retry button; user retries and the table successfully renders rows.
flows.name: Handle data fetch error with retry

steps.action: Navigate to the transactions list view during a network/server failure for the transactions fetch.
steps.expectedResult: Table header renders; table enters Error state after the failed fetch.

steps.action: Observe the table error state.
steps.expectedResult: A full-width row/message displays "Transactions couldn’t be loaded" with a visible "Retry" button; sorting and pagination controls are disabled until data loads successfully.

steps.action: Click the Retry button.
steps.expectedResult: A new fetch is triggered; table shows loading skeleton placeholders and keeps header visible; controls remain disabled during loading.

steps.action: Wait for the retry fetch to succeed.
steps.expectedResult: Error message is replaced by transaction rows; default sort Date descending is applied unless a persisted sort exists; pagination appears if needed and becomes interactive.
