Apply aria-sort on the corresponding <th> with values \"none\" (unsorted), \"ascending\", or \"descending\"; only the actively sorted column has ascending/descending and all others are \"none\".","rationale":"This defines a complete keyboard interaction and a standards-based announcement of sort state without changing the visual design requirements, enabling accessible sorting for all columns.","sourceGap":"Define keyboard interaction for sortable headers (tab focus, Enter/Space to sort) and announce sort state via aria-sort"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"row_details_accessible_action","decision":"Make the first cell in each row (Date) contain a full-row overlay anchor link styled to cover the row hit area. The link navigates to a details route pattern \"/transactions/{transactionId}\". The link accessible name is \"View transaction {transactionId}\". Preserve standard link behaviors (keyboard Enter, open in new tab via context menu/middle click).","rationale":"Using a real link provides a clear, keyboard-accessible affordance for opening details and supports common navigation expectations conservatively without inventing a modal/drawer pattern.","sourceGap":"Row click opens details but no accessible affordance is defined (e.g., row as link/button with role and accessible name) or alternative action for keyboard users"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"pagination_controls_labels_and_focus","decision":"Pagination includes: Previous button, Next button, and a page size <select> with options 25/50/100. Wrap controls in a <nav aria-label=\"Transaction table pagination\">. Previous/Next have aria-label \"Previous page\" / \"Next page\" and use disabled=true at boundaries. Render current page text \"Page X of Y\" as an aria-live=\"polite\" region that updates on page changes. Tab order is Previous -> Next -> Page size selector.","rationale":"This specifies explicit labels, boundary disabled behavior, and a deterministic focus order while keeping the UI minimal and consistent with the brief (no requirement for page numbers/first/last).","sourceGap":"Pagination controls need explicit labeling for screen readers (current page, next/previous, page size selector) and focus order behavior"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_status_badge"],"code":"status_badge_text_not_color_only","decision":"Always render the status text inside the badge (e.g., \"Pending\"). The badge element includes aria-label identical to the visible text. Do not rely on color to convey meaning; color is supplementary only.","rationale":"Keeping status text present ensures non-visual users receive the same information and resolves the risk of color-only encoding without requiring extra UI elements.","sourceGap":"Status conveyed by color only is possible; specify text/aria-label remains present and ensure badge meaning is announced non-visually"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table","transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"focus_visible_styles","decision":"Apply a consistent focus-visible ring to interactive elements: sortable header buttons, row overlay links, pagination buttons, and the page size select. Use a 2px outline with 2px offset and ensure it is visible on all status badge background colors.","rationale":"Explicit focus-visible styling ensures keyboard usability across all interactive controls without prescribing a full theme, and it is a conservative accessibility baseline.","sourceGap":"Specify focus-visible styling for interactive elements (headers, rows, pagination) to meet keyboard usability"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"loading_empty_error_states","decision":"Add three table-level states: (1) Loading: show 10-row skeleton placeholders while retaining the table header; disable sorting and pagination controls. (2) Empty: show a single full-width row message \"No transactions\"; keep headers visible and hide pagination. (3) Error: show a full-width message \"Transactions couldn’t be loaded\" with a \"Retry\" button that re-triggers fetch; keep headers visible and disable sorting/pagination until success.","rationale":"These states cover the primary data lifecycle gaps (loading/empty/error) in a way that preserves layout stability and defines control availability for downstream implementation and tests.","sourceGap":"Loading state for initial fetch and for sort/pagination transitions (skeleton/placeholder vs spinner)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"sort_behavior_defaults_and_nulls","decision":"Default sort is Date descending. Sorting is bi-state per column: selecting a column toggles ascending/descending; selecting a different column activates that column in ascending order. Sorting is stable. Null/blank values always sort last in both directions.","rationale":"This fully specifies predictable sort rules (default, toggling, stability, null handling) with conservative choices commonly used in transaction tables.","sourceGap":"Define sorting rules per column: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggling, stable sort behavior, and how null/blank values sort"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"pagination_page_size_change_resets","decision":"When page size changes (25/50/100), reset to page 1 and refetch/recompute the dataset for that new size. Keep the current sort applied.","rationale":"Resetting to page 1 prevents out-of-range pages after size changes and preserves the user’s chosen ordering, minimizing surprises and edge cases.","sourceGap":"Define pagination UI specifics: which controls appear (prev/next, first/last, page numbers), where the 25/50/100 selector lives, and whether page resets to 1 when page size changes"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"column_formats_and_alignment","decision":"Date displays as \"YYYY-MM-DD\" in the user’s local timezone. Amount displays as a currency formatted using the user locale with two decimal places; negative amounts display with a leading minus sign. Align Amount right; all other columns left.","rationale":"This resolves formatting and alignment ambiguities with locale-safe defaults and conventional financial table alignment without requiring additional inputs.","sourceGap":"Specify table column data formats and alignment rules: date format/timezone, currency formatting for amount, right/left alignment, and negative/zero handling"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_status_badge"],"code":"status_to_style_mapping_and_unknown_fallback","decision":"Map statuses to badge styles: pending=amber, completed=green, failed=red, refunded=blue. Set minimum widths: Date 120px, Amount 120px, Status 120px, Merchant Name 200px, Payment Method 160px. accessibilityGaps: Sorting controls lack keyboard interaction and screen-reader semantics (which headers are buttons, current sort column/direction, aria-sort)
Row click to open details lacks an accessible affordance (keyboard activation, focusability, and clear label for screen readers)
Status badges rely on color; no non-color reinforcement specified beyond text and no guidance for contrast-compliant badge/background pairings
Pagination controls lack labeling for screen readers (current page, total pages/results, page size selector label) and focus order expectations
No focus-visible styling requirements specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls
missingStates: Loading state while fetching transactions (initial load and during sort/paginate)
Empty state when there are no transactions to display
Error state when transactions fail to load or pagination/sort request fails, including retry behavior
Disabled states for pagination controls at boundaries (first/prev on first page, next/last on last page)
Active/selected state for the currently sorted column header and sort direction indicator
Row hover/active/selected state to indicate clickability and current focus/selection
Long-content overflow state for merchant name and payment method (truncate/wrap) and tooltip behavior if used
recommendations: Define sort behavior precisely: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggle, stable sort, and visual indicator (icon) placement in headers
Specify table data formatting rules: date format/timezone, amount currency/precision/negative styling, and canonical labels for payment method values

Make row navigation accessible by using a dedicated primary cell link or making the row a focusable element with Enter/Space activation and an explicit accessible name (e.g., 'View transaction details for {merchant} on {date}')
Add explicit ARIA patterns: aria-sort on headers, aria-live announcement for sort/page changes, and labels for page size selector and pagination buttons
Define badge design tokens and contrast requirements per status (text color, background color, border) to ensure WCAG-compliant contrast
Specify pagination model: show total count, page count, and whether page size change resets to page 1; define available controls (first/prev/next/last, direct page input) and their labels
Add system states and UI treatments: skeleton rows/spinner for loading, empty/error messaging copy, and retry action placement
responsiveGaps: No behavior defined for small screens: whether the table becomes horizontally scrollable, columns collapse, or transforms into a stacked/card layout
Column priority not specified for responsive collapse/hide (which columns can be hidden first and how users access hidden data)
No truncation/wrapping rules for narrow widths (merchant name and payment method) and how that impacts row height
Pagination layout on mobile not specified (stacking of page controls and page-size selector, tap target sizing)
No specification for sticky header or scroll containment when the table overflows vertically or horizontally

coveredBehaviors: Composed table workflow: loading skeleton disables sorting and pagination then renders rows
Default sort state reflected via aria-sort on active <th> only (Date descending) and other headers omit aria-sort
Sorting across components: clicking a sortable header triggers parent reload; controls disabled while loading; aria-live announces sort change; final render reflects new sort
Pagination across components: Next page triggers reload; aria-live announces page change; boundary enablement updates on page > 1
Page size change resets to page 1 and triggers reload; pagination summary updates; aria-live announces the new page
Row-level navigation: dedicated 'View details' control opens details via callback (keyboard Enter) with accessible name pattern
Error recovery: sort triggers fetch error; error row with Retry blocks interactions; Retry recovers to loaded rows without crashing
Overflow compatibility: Merchant Name and Payment Method cells expose full value via title attribute

decisions.decision: Render each sortable column header as a native <button> within the <th>; the button label is the column name. Set aria-sort on the <th> for the active sort column only (values: "ascending" or "descending"); all other headers omit aria-sort. Keyboard: Enter/Space toggles sort. Provide a visible sort indicator icon adjacent to the header text inside the button.
decisions.rationale: Using native buttons provides built-in keyboard and focus behavior without custom key handling. aria-sort on the <th> communicates current sort state to assistive tech in the standard table pattern, and limiting aria-sort to the active column avoids conflicting announcements.
decisions.sourceGap: Sorting controls lack keyboard interaction and screen-reader semantics (which headers are buttons, current sort column/direction, aria-sort)

decisions.decision: Default sort is Date descending. Sorting is bi-state per column: activating a different column sets direction to ascending; activating the same column toggles between ascending and descending. Sorting is stable (preserves input order for equal values).
decisions.rationale: This resolves ambiguity around default and toggle model while staying conservative and predictable for users. Stable sorting avoids unexpected row reordering when values tie.
decisions.sourceGap: Define sort behavior precisely: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggle, stable sort, and visual indicator (icon) placement in headers

decisions.decision: Do not make the entire row the only interactive control. Add a dedicated "View details" link/button in the first cell (Date column) for each row; it is keyboard focusable and activates on Enter/Space. The accessible name is "View transaction details for {merchantName} on {date}". Row click may still activate details with pointer, but keyboard users use the dedicated control.
decisions.rationale: A dedicated interactive element provides clear semantics, focusability, and a screen-reader label without turning <tr> into a custom control. Allowing pointer row-click preserves the brief behavior while ensuring full keyboard accessibility.
decisions.sourceGap: Row click to open details lacks an accessible affordance (keyboard activation, focusability, and clear label for screen readers)

decisions.decision: Implement three explicit render states in the table body: (1) Loading: show 10 skeleton rows matching the current column layout and disable sorting/pagination controls; (2) Empty: show a single full-width row with message "No transactions to display"; (3) Error: show a single full-width row with message "Transactions failed to load" and a "Retry" button that re-triggers the last fetch with current sort/page/pageSize.
decisions.rationale: These states cover the missing operational scenarios (fetching, no data, failure) with concrete UI outputs and control behavior, enabling deterministic tests and consistent UX across sort/paginate transitions.
decisions.sourceGap: Loading state while fetching transactions (initial load and during sort/paginate)

decisions.decision: Pagination provides First, Previous, Next, Last buttons plus a page size selector (25/50/100). Display text: "Page X of Y" and "Z results". Changing page size resets to page 1. First/Previous are disabled on page 1; Next/Last are disabled on the final page. Disabled controls are not focusable.
decisions.rationale: This fixes boundary behavior and defines a concrete pagination model and reset rule, keeping the control set minimal while supporting the required page sizes and clear user feedback.
decisions.sourceGap: Specify pagination model: show total count, page count, and whether page size change resets to page 1; define available controls (first/prev/next/last, direct page input) and their labels

decisions.decision: Add accessible labels: pagination nav has aria-label "Transaction pagination"; page size selector has label "Rows per page"; First/Prev/Next/Last buttons have aria-labels "First page", "Previous page", "Next page", "Last page". Add an aria-live="polite" status region within the table container that announces "Sorted by {column} {direction}" on sort and "Page {x} of {y}" on page changes.
decisions.rationale: Explicit labeling and polite announcements address screen-reader discoverability and feedback for dynamic updates without overcomplicating the interaction model.
decisions.sourceGap: Pagination controls lack labeling for screen readers (current page, total pages/results, page size selector label) and focus order expectations

decisions.decision: Apply consistent :focus-visible styling to sortable header buttons, the "View details" control, and all pagination controls: 2px outline using the app focus color, 2px offset, and maintain at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Do not remove default outlines unless replaced by this rule.
decisions.rationale: This creates a concrete, testable focus requirement for all interactive elements mentioned in the gaps and avoids relying on browser defaults that may be overridden by component styling.
decisions.sourceGap: No focus-visible styling requirements specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls

decisions.decision: Badges always render the status text (Pending/Completed/Failed/Refunded) and must meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for text against badge background (>=4.5:1). If a chosen background cannot meet contrast with the intended text color, use a neutral background with a 2px left border in the status color and standard text color to preserve meaning without relying on low-contrast fills.
decisions.rationale: Text provides non-color reinforcement, and the contrast rule plus fallback prevents inaccessible color pairings while preserving status differentiation in a conservative way.
decisions.sourceGap: Status badges rely on color; no non-color reinforcement specified beyond text and no guidance for contrast-compliant badge/background pairings

decisions.decision: Merchant Name and Payment Method cells are single-line with truncation (CSS ellipsis). On hover and keyboard focus (within cell), show a native tooltip via title attribute containing the full value. Row height remains fixed to a single line.
decisions.rationale: This defines deterministic overflow handling on narrow widths without introducing complex custom tooltip components, and it remains accessible via focus-triggered title for keyboard users.
decisions.sourceGap: Long-content overflow state for merchant name and payment method (truncate/wrap) and tooltip behavior if used

decisions.decision: On small screens, keep the table layout and enable horizontal scrolling within the table container (overflow-x: auto). Columns remain in the same order and are not hidden; minimum widths: Date 120px, Amount 120px, Status 120px, Merchant Name 200px, Payment Method 160px.
decisions.rationale: Horizontal scroll is the least risky responsive strategy for a data table because it preserves all data and interactions without inventing a card layout or column hiding behavior not specified in the brief.
decisions.sourceGap: No behavior defined for small screens: whether the table becomes horizontally scrollable, columns collapse, or transforms into a stacked/card layout

coveredBehaviors: Renders the correct human-readable label for each supported status (pending/completed/failed/refunded)
Exposes status text in the accessible name (not color-only meaning)
Applies a status-specific styling hook (via class or data attribute) so status can be colored by CSS
Merges optional class_name with the component's base styling hook
Renders all required column headers (Date, Amount, Status, Merchant Name, Payment Method) as sortable header buttons

When transactions is empty and not loading/error, renders the empty state message

Merchant Name and Payment Method cells include title attributes with full text for native tooltip on truncation rule

Loading state: skeleton rows and disabled controls

coveredBehaviors: Renders accessible pagination landmark with aria-label "Transaction pagination"
Displays "Page X of Y" computed from total_results and page_size (ceil)
Displays "Z results" reflecting total_results
First/Previous buttons request page 1 / page-1; Next/Last request page+1 / totalPages

Rows-per-page selector is labeled "Rows per page"

flows.name: Open transaction details from the first row

steps.action: Land on the page containing the transaction table and wait for the initial fetch to complete.
steps.expectedResult: Table initially shows loading skeleton rows with sorting and pagination disabled; then renders rows sorted by Date descending with status badges visible and pagination showing "Page 1 of Y" and "Z results".

steps.action: Activate the "View details" control in the first row (in the Date column).
steps.expectedResult: Transaction details open for the selected transaction; the control has an accessible name "View transaction details for {merchantName} on {date}".

flows.completionCriteria: User successfully sorts, paginates, changes page size (resetting to page 1), and opens details for a transaction.
flows.name: Explore sorting, pagination, page size, truncation tooltip, then open details

steps.action: Wait for the table to load and confirm default sort state.
steps.expectedResult: Rows are sorted by Date descending; the Date header <th> has aria-sort="descending" and displays a visible sort indicator icon; aria-sort is not present on other headers.

steps.action: Click the Amount column header button to sort by Amount.
steps.expectedResult: Table enters loading state (skeleton rows) with sorting/pagination disabled; then renders sorted by Amount ascending (stable for equal values). aria-live announces "Sorted by Amount ascending"; Amount header <th> has aria-sort="ascending" and the indicator updates.

steps.action: Activate the Amount column header button again to toggle direction.
steps.expectedResult: Table reloads and then renders sorted by Amount descending; aria-live announces "Sorted by Amount descending"; Amount header aria-sort updates to "descending".

steps.action: Click Next page in the pagination controls.
steps.expectedResult: Table reloads and then shows Page 2 results; aria-live announces "Page 2 of Y"; First/Previous become enabled (and focusable) while on page > 1.

steps.action: Change page size to 100 using the Rows per page selector.
steps.expectedResult: Page resets to 1; table reloads and then shows 100 rows (or fewer if total results < 100); pagination updates "Page 1 of Y" and "Z results"; aria-live announces "Page 1 of Y".

steps.action: Hover over a truncated Merchant Name cell to view the full value (or focus the cell content via keyboard).
steps.expectedResult: Cell remains single-line with ellipsis; the browser-native tooltip appears via the title attribute showing the full Merchant Name value.

steps.action: Use keyboard Tab to focus the "View details" control for a visible row and press Enter.
steps.expectedResult: A clear :focus-visible outline is shown on the focused control; pressing Enter opens transaction details for that row using the accessible name pattern.

flows.completionCriteria: After a failed fetch, the user successfully retries and the table renders rows.
flows.name: Sort triggers fetch error; user retries to recover

steps.action: Click the Payment Method column header button to request sorting by Payment Method.
steps.expectedResult: Table enters loading state with skeleton rows and disables sorting/pagination while the request is in flight.

steps.action: Observe the request failure state.
steps.expectedResult: Table body renders a single full-width error row with message "Transactions failed to load" and a "Retry" button; previous data is not interactable; sorting/pagination remain disabled until a successful reload.

steps.action: Click the "Retry" button in the error row.
steps.expectedResult: The last fetch is re-triggered using the current sort/page/pageSize; table shows loading skeleton rows with controls disabled, then renders the transaction rows if the retry succeeds.

flows.completionCriteria: Empty state is displayed with the specified message when there are no transactions.
flows.name: No transactions available shows empty state

steps.action: Load the transaction table when the dataset is empty.
steps.expectedResult: After loading completes, the table body renders a single full-width row with message "No transactions to display"; pagination reflects "Z results" where Z=0 and boundary buttons are disabled and not focusable.

component.business_context: Viewing and managing a list of financial transactions.
component.name: Transaction Table

constraints: Supports pagination with page sizes 25, 50, or 100 items per page.

accessibility_gaps: Sorting controls lack keyboard interaction and screen-reader semantics (which headers are buttons, current sort column/direction, aria-sort)
Row click to open details lacks an accessible affordance (keyboard activation, focusability, and clear label for screen readers)
Status badges rely on color; no non-color reinforcement specified beyond text and no guidance for contrast-compliant badge/background pairings
Pagination controls lack labeling for screen readers (current page, total pages/results, page size selector label) and focus order expectations
No focus-visible styling requirements specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls
missing_states: Loading state while fetching transactions (initial load and during sort/paginate)
Empty state when there are no transactions to display
Error state when transactions fail to load or pagination/sort request fails, including retry behavior
Disabled states for pagination controls at boundaries (first/prev on first page, next/last on last page)
Active/selected state for the currently sorted column header and sort direction indicator
Row hover/active/selected state to indicate clickability and current focus/selection
Long-content overflow state for merchant name and payment method (truncate/wrap) and tooltip behavior if used
recommendations: Define sort behavior precisely: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggle, stable sort, and visual indicator (icon) placement in headers
Specify table data formatting rules: date format/timezone, amount currency/precision/negative styling, and canonical labels for payment method values

Make row navigation accessible by using a dedicated primary cell link or making the row a focusable element with Enter/Space activation and an explicit accessible name (e.g., 'View transaction details for {merchant} on {date}')
Add explicit ARIA patterns: aria-sort on headers, aria-live announcement for sort/page changes, and labels for page size selector and pagination buttons
Define badge design tokens and contrast requirements per status (text color, background color, border) to ensure WCAG-compliant contrast
Specify pagination model: show total count, page count, and whether page size change resets to page 1; define available controls (first/prev/next/last, direct page input) and their labels
Add system states and UI treatments: skeleton rows/spinner for loading, empty/error messaging copy, and retry action placement
responsive_gaps: No behavior defined for small screens: whether the table becomes horizontally scrollable, columns collapse, or transforms into a stacked/card layout
Column priority not specified for responsive collapse/hide (which columns can be hidden first and how users access hidden data)
No truncation/wrapping rules for narrow widths (merchant name and payment method) and how that impacts row height
Pagination layout on mobile not specified (stacking of page controls and page-size selector, tap target sizing)
No specification for sticky header or scroll containment when the table overflows vertically or horizontally

{
  "accessibilityGaps": [
    "Sorting controls lack keyboard interaction and screen-reader semantics (which headers are buttons, current sort column/direction, aria-sort)",

    "Active/selected state for the currently sorted column header and sort direction indicator",
    "Row hover/active/selected state to indicate clickability and current focus/selection",
    "Long-content overflow state for merchant name and payment method (truncate/wrap) and tooltip behavior if used"
  ],

    "Define sort behavior precisely: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggle, stable sort, and visual indicator (icon) placement in headers",
    "Specify table data formatting rules: date format/timezone, amount currency/precision/negative styling, and canonical labels for payment method values",
    "Make row navigation accessible by using a dedicated primary cell link or making the row a focusable element with Enter/Space activation and an explicit accessible name (e.g., 'View transaction details for {merchant} on {date}')",

    "Define badge design tokens and contrast requirements per status (text color, background color, border) to ensure WCAG-compliant contrast",
    "Specify pagination model: show total count, page count, and whether page size change resets to page 1; define available controls (first/prev/next/last, direct page input) and their labels",

steps.inputJson: {"componentDescription":"Transaction table with columns: date, amount, status, merchant name, payment method. Supports sorting by any column and pagination (25/50/100 per page). Status values: pending, completed, failed, refunded. Each status has a colored badge. Row click opens transaction details."}
steps.outputJson: {"decisions":[{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"sortable_header_button_semantics","decision":"Render each sortable column header as a native <button> within the <th>; the button label is the column name. Set aria-sort on the <th> for the active sort column only (values: \"ascending\" or \"descending\"); all other headers omit aria-sort. Keyboard: Enter/Space toggles sort. Provide a visible sort indicator icon adjacent to the header text inside the button.","rationale":"Using native buttons provides built-in keyboard and focus behavior without custom key handling. aria-sort on the <th> communicates current sort state to assistive tech in the standard table pattern, and limiting aria-sort to the active column avoids conflicting announcements.","sourceGap":"Sorting controls lack keyboard interaction and screen-reader semantics (which headers are buttons, current sort column/direction, aria-sort)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"sort_toggle_and_default","decision":"Default sort is Date descending. Sorting is bi-state per column: activating a different column sets direction to ascending; activating the same column toggles between ascending and descending. Sorting is stable (preserves input order for equal values).","rationale":"This resolves ambiguity around default and toggle model while staying conservative and predictable for users. Stable sorting avoids unexpected row reordering when values tie.","sourceGap":"Define sort behavior precisely: default sort column/direction, tri-state vs bi-state toggle, stable sort, and visual indicator (icon) placement in headers"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"row_details_accessible_affordance","decision":"Do not make the entire row the only interactive control. Add a dedicated \"View details\" link/button in the first cell (Date column) for each row; it is keyboard focusable and activates on Enter/Space. The accessible name is \"View transaction details for {merchantName} on {date}\". Row click may still activate details with pointer, but keyboard users use the dedicated control.","rationale":"A dedicated interactive element provides clear semantics, focusability, and a screen-reader label without turning <tr> into a custom control. Allowing pointer row-click preserves the brief behavior while ensuring full keyboard accessibility.","sourceGap":"Row click to open details lacks an accessible affordance (keyboard activation, focusability, and clear label for screen readers)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"table_loading_empty_error_states","decision":"Implement three explicit render states in the table body: (1) Loading: show 10 skeleton rows matching the current column layout and disable sorting/pagination controls; (2) Empty: show a single full-width row with message \"No transactions to display\"; (3) Error: show a single full-width row with message \"Transactions failed to load\" and a \"Retry\" button that re-triggers the last fetch with current sort/page/pageSize.","rationale":"These states cover the missing operational scenarios (fetching, no data, failure) with concrete UI outputs and control behavior, enabling deterministic tests and consistent UX across sort/paginate transitions.","sourceGap":"Loading state while fetching transactions (initial load and during sort/paginate)"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"pagination_model_and_disabled_boundaries","decision":"Pagination provides First, Previous, Next, Last buttons plus a page size selector (25/50/100). Display text: \"Page X of Y\" and \"Z results\". Changing page size resets to page 1. First/Previous are disabled on page 1; Next/Last are disabled on the final page. Disabled controls are not focusable.","rationale":"This fixes boundary behavior and defines a concrete pagination model and reset rule, keeping the control set minimal while supporting the required page sizes and clear user feedback.","sourceGap":"Specify pagination model: show total count, page count, and whether page size change resets to page 1; define available controls (first/prev/next/last, direct page input) and their labels"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"pagination_accessible_labels_and_live_updates","decision":"Add accessible labels: pagination nav has aria-label \"Transaction pagination\"; page size selector has label \"Rows per page\"; First/Prev/Next/Last buttons have aria-labels \"First page\", \"Previous page\", \"Next page\", \"Last page\". Add an aria-live=\"polite\" status region within the table container that announces \"Sorted by {column} {direction}\" on sort and \"Page {x} of {y}\" on page changes.","rationale":"Explicit labeling and polite announcements address screen-reader discoverability and feedback for dynamic updates without overcomplicating the interaction model.","sourceGap":"Pagination controls lack labeling for screen readers (current page, total pages/results, page size selector label) and focus order expectations"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table","transaction_table_pagination"],"code":"focus_visible_requirements","decision":"Apply consistent :focus-visible styling to sortable header buttons, the \"View details\" control, and all pagination controls: 2px outline using the app focus color, 2px offset, and maintain at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Do not remove default outlines unless replaced by this rule.","rationale":"This creates a concrete, testable focus requirement for all interactive elements mentioned in the gaps and avoids relying on browser defaults that may be overridden by component styling.","sourceGap":"No focus-visible styling requirements specified for sortable headers, rows, and pagination controls"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table_status_badge"],"code":"status_badge_contrast_and_noncolor_redundancy","decision":"Badges always render the status text (Pending/Completed/Failed/Refunded) and must meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for text against badge background (>=4.5:1). If a chosen background cannot meet contrast with the intended text color, use a neutral background with a 2px left border in the status color and standard text color to preserve meaning without relying on low-contrast fills.","rationale":"Text provides non-color reinforcement, and the contrast rule plus fallback prevents inaccessible color pairings while preserving status differentiation in a conservative way.","sourceGap":"Status badges rely on color; no non-color reinforcement specified beyond text and no guidance for contrast-compliant badge/background pairings"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"cell_overflow_truncation_rules","decision":"Merchant Name and Payment Method cells are single-line with truncation (CSS ellipsis). On hover and keyboard focus (within cell), show a native tooltip via title attribute containing the full value. Row height remains fixed to a single line.","rationale":"This defines deterministic overflow handling on narrow widths without introducing complex custom tooltip components, and it remains accessible via focus-triggered title for keyboard users.","sourceGap":"Long-content overflow state for merchant name and payment method (truncate/wrap) and tooltip behavior if used"},{"affectedComponentCodes":["transaction_table"],"code":"responsive_table_horizontal_scroll_and_column_priority","decision":"On small screens, keep the table layout and enable horizontal scrolling within the table container (overflow-x: auto). Columns remain in the same order and are not hidden; minimum widths: Date 120px, Amount 120px, Status 120px, Merchant Name 200px, Payment Method 160px.","rationale":"Horizontal scroll is the least risky responsive strategy for a data table because it preserves all data and interactions without inventing a card layout or column hiding behavior not specified in the brief.","sourceGap":"No behavior defined for small screens: whether the table becomes horizontally scrollable, columns collapse, or transforms into a stacked/card layout"}]}
